gm.title: Description
lines: The aboleth spreads slime pox through close contact and uses ancient memories as a psychic weapon.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 20, Stealth 9. Resists acid. Immune to psychic damage. Darkvision 120 ft. Deep Speech and telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +5, Dex −1, Con +6, Int +8, Wis +6, Cha +4.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Aberrant Resilience. Resistance to Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed and Stunned. Advantage on saves against effects that alter its form.
Amphibious. The aboleth breathes in air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). After failing a save, it can choose to succeed.
Probing Telepathy. It learns the greatest desires of a creature it can see if that creature communicates with it telepathically.
Slime Pox. The infected creature can breathe in air and water, can regain HP only underwater, and takes 6 (1d12) acid damage for every hour it stays out of water or its skin goes without added moisture. Every 24 hours, make a DC 16 Charisma save. After three failures it becomes the aboleth’s protective thrall. After three successes it remains infected and autonomous. The results need not be consecutive. Stop making saves when one outcome is reached. Only heal or similar magic cures the disease.
Slimy Skin. Touching the aboleth or hitting it in melee from 5 ft. or closer requires a DC 16 Constitution save against Slime Pox.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Tentacle and Psychic Bolt. If two tentacle attacks hit the same target, it makes a DC 16 Constitution save against Slime Pox.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning.
Psychic Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +8 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit 14 (3d6 + 4) psychic.
Psychic Torrent (recharge 5–6). Up to three visible creatures within 60 ft. each make a DC 16 Wisdom save. On a failure, take 49 (14d6) psychic damage and become Incapacitated through the end of the target’s next turn. A success halves the damage and prevents the condition.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Three actions per round, regained at the start of the aboleth’s turn. Use one option at the end of another creature’s turn. The aboleth cannot use these while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Detect (1 action). Pinpoint every creature and trap within 60 ft. automatically.
Swim (1 action). Swim up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Slime Drain (2 actions). One creature with Slime Pox within 30 ft. takes 10 (3d6) acid damage. The aboleth regains HP equal to the damage dealt.

lines: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2, p. 236.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: Adam is a flesh golem built by Victor Mordenheim and the darklord of Lamordia. He keeps to the Isle of Agony and longs to be human.

gm.title: Shared curse
lines: Adam feels wounds inflicted on Victor Mordenheim. He hates his creator and cannot bring himself to harm him.

gm.title: Combat
lines: Mundane weapons do not hurt him. A weapon needs a +1 or better enchantment to hit.
Natural cold and electricity cannot harm him. Their magical equivalents deal half damage. Nondamaging spells restore 1 hit point per spell level when absorbed.
He has an 80% chance to hide in shadows, move silently, detect noise or climb walls. His speed halves while moving silently. He can feign being affected by a spell to escape or set up an ambush.

gm.title: Closing the borders
lines: Adam can raise a blizzard to force anyone trying to leave Lamordia back into the domain.

gm.title: Description
lines: An arcane construct bound into a mithral mask by a spellwright.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Strength saves +11, Dexterity +8. Athletics +11, Perception +7. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 17. Understands its creator’s languages but cannot speak. Natural armor. Resists damage from spells. Immune to poison damage and to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks. Immune to Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified and Poisoned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Arcane Nature. It can function without air, food, drink or sleep.
Immutable Form. Its shape cannot be changed by magic or other effects.
Magic Resistance. It rolls saves against spells and other magical effects with Advantage.
Magic Weapons. Treat its weapon attacks as magical.
Arcane Leak. Once reduced to half its maximum HP (85), its mask cracks. A creature that starts its turn within 10 ft. of it or first enters that radius on a turn takes 10 (3d6) radiant damage. Casting in the radius requires a DC 14 check with the caster’s spellcasting ability. On failure the spell fails, the slot is expended, and the caster takes 3 (1d6) force damage per slot level.
Powerful Build. Treat it as one size larger for carrying, pushing, dragging and lifting.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Claws attacks.
Claws. Melee weapon attack +11, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 32 (4d12 + 6) slashing.
Force Bolts (Recharge 5–6). Choose up to four creatures it can see within 60 ft. Each takes 28 (8d6) force damage on a failed DC 18 Dexterity save.

gm.title: Customization
lines:
Most adranachs have one optional feature. Most masters have three.
Advanced Tracking (once per long rest). When a creature fails its Force Bolts save, it may mark the creature for 24 hours. On the same plane, the adranach knows the direction to the creature and which way it is moving.
Arcane Bond. Its creator can speak with it telepathically within 1 mile. The creator may spend an action to use the adranach’s hearing and sight, including its special senses, until the creator’s next turn starts. The creator is Blinded and Deafened to their own surroundings during that time.
Slipstream. It can cast Invisibility on itself at will. Double its speed while Invisible.
Master only · Astral Form (once per long rest). Cast Astral Projection on itself.
Master only · Truesight. It has Truesight to 30 ft. It can spend an action to extend that range to 120 ft. through the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: The Master Adranach has its own combat profile.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed Charisma modifier is +1 for a score of 11. The ability grid uses the standard +0. The book does not specify how Arcane Leak handles a spell cast without a slot.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Magic Resistance. The archmage has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. Spellcasting. The archmage is an 18th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks). The archmage can cast disguise self and invisibility at will and has the following wizard spells prepared: Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, light, mage hand, prestidigitation, shocking grasp 1st level (4 slots): detect magic, identify, mage armor,* magic missile 2nd level (3 slots): detect thoughts, mirror image, misty step 3rd level (3 slots): counterspell, fly, lightning bolt 4th level (3 slots): banishment, fire shield, stoneskin* 5th level (3 slots): cone of cold, scrying, wall of force 6th level (1 slot): globe of invulnerability 7th level (1 slot): teleport 8th level (1 slot): mind blank* 9th level (1 slot): time stop *The archmage casts these spells on itself before combat. Fey Ancestry. Advantage on saves against charm. Magical sleep fails.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Dagger. Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage. Archmages are powerful (and usually quite old) spellcasters dedicated to the study of the arcane arts. Benevolent ones counsel kings and queens, while evil ones rule as tyrants and pursue lichdom. Those who are neither good nor evil sequester themselves in remote towers to practice their magic without interruption. An archmage typically has one or more apprentice mages, and an archmage’s abode has numerous magical wards and guardians to discourage interlopers.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Fury shared rules
lines:
Printed source. Furies, pp. 79–80. The sisters appear together and speak all humanoid languages. They try three times to divert a target from atonement before trying to kill them in public.
Defenses. Damage reduction 15/good. Immune to paralysis, polymorph, and mind-affecting effects.
Scourge. The +3 scourge works like a whip that deals 1d4 lethal damage before modifiers. A Fury may substitute it for her claw attacks. Use the attack and ability damage listed for that sister. Rake (Ex) is +9 melee for 1d4 + 1 damage.
Alter Self (Sp). At will as a standard action, a Fury can take the form of an elderly human woman indefinitely. Caster level 10.
Breath Weapon (Su, 3/day). Fill one adjacent square with foul air. Apply stinking cloud as cast by an 8th-level sorcerer, with a DC 16 Fortitude save.
Find Penitent (Su). Furies can locate a target who seeks redemption at the invitation or embrace stage of corruption. The target cannot hide from them, even with magic.
Gaseous Death (Su). At 0 HP, a Fury and her scourge dissolve into smoke. Surviving sisters continue to fight, though the last survivor tries to flee. If a sister survives, the slain Furies return at full HP after 24 hours. To kill them permanently, all three must die within the same 24 hours and an Innocent must deal the killing blows. Their scourges remain after permanent death.
Weaknesses. A good cleric or a paladin can turn each Fury separately by invoking her true name. A turning attempt cannot destroy, rebuke, or command her. A Fury cannot deliberately harm a good creature except with her breath weapon.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The stat block calls the scourge’s effect Wisdom drain and gives a ranged attack, while the combat text calls the effect Wisdom damage and the shared rules treat scourges as whips. Use the printed attack bonus and the specific Wisdom-damage procedure. The attack line calls it scourge of fools. The listed Dexterity score also differs from the Dexterity bonus printed in AC.

lines:
Multiattack. Use Contaminating Presence and make three Tentacle attacks. Any of those attacks can be replaced with Fling.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +17, reach 5 ft., one target, 23 (3d8 + 10) piercing. A Large or smaller target already Grappled by the amalgamation is Swallowed, ending that grapple. Inside, it is Blinded and Restrained, has total cover from outside, takes 42 (12d6) acid damage, and gains one level of Contamination at the start of the amalgamation's turns. If the amalgamation takes 50 or more damage in a single turn from a creature inside it, it makes a DC 25 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On a failure all swallowed creatures fall Prone within 10 ft. If it dies, they cease to be Restrained and can spend 15 ft. of movement to exit Prone.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack +17, reach 50 ft., one target, 20 (3d6 + 10) bludgeoning. Grapple the target (escape DC 18). It is Restrained while grappled. Each of twelve tentacles can hold one target.
Fling. Throw one Large or smaller held object or grappled creature up to 60 ft. A thrown creature lands Prone. Against a solid surface, it takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning per 10 ft. thrown. A creature the target is thrown at must pass a DC 18 Dexterity save or take the same damage and fall Prone.
Mind-breaking Whispers. One creature within 120 ft. must pass a DC 20 Intelligence save or take 35 (10d6) psychic damage and become insane until it finishes a long rest. It cannot take actions, understand speech, or read, and can only speak gibberish. Greater Restoration ends the effect.
Contaminating Presence. Each humanoid within 120 ft. must pass a DC 20 Constitution save or take 10 (3d6) necrotic damage and gain one level of Contamination.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines:
Three legendary actions per round. Use one option after another creature's turn and recover spent actions at the start of this creature's turn.
Tentacle Attack or Fling. Use either option.
Mind-breaking Whispers (2 actions). Use Mind-breaking Whispers.
Piper at the Gate (3 actions). Summon up to five gibbering mouthers into empty spaces within 30 ft. They obey the amalgamation, act immediately after it on the same initiative count, and remain until destroyed. It can have at most ten mouthers summoned by this action.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Description
lines: Kel Belleth turned her exile into a base for the Void. She recruits disaffected celestials and aids cults from her demiplane, Sun Hollow.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 20, Stealth 14. Immune to necrotic damage. Truesight 120 ft. Speaks all languages and has telepathy 120 ft. CR 16 in Sun Hollow.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: STR +7 · DEX +4 · CON +11 · INT +4 · WIS +10 · CHA +10

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Angelic Resilience. Resist radiant damage and damage from nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing attacks. Immune to Exhaustion, Charmed, and Frightened.
Angelic Senses. Pinpoint Aberrations, Celestials, Fiends, and Undead within 30 ft. Recognize consecration or desecration on any place or object the angel can sense.
Divine Awareness. Kel Belleth recognizes any lie she hears.
Divine Protection. Aberrations, Celestials, Fiends, and Undead roll attacks against her with disadvantage.
Immortal Nature. The angel needs no food, drink, or sleep.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). She can choose to succeed when she fails a save.
Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Void Weapons. Her weapon attacks are magical and add 4d8 necrotic damage on a hit, as included below.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Greatsword attacks or four Void Bolt attacks. One attack in either set can be replaced with Chain.
Greatsword. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 28 (6d6 + 7) slashing plus 18 (4d8) necrotic damage.
Chain. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning plus 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. Grapple the target (escape DC 18) and Restrain it until the grapple ends. Each of her three chains can hold one target.
Void Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +10 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit 23 (4d8 + 5) necrotic damage.
Soul Siphon (Recharge 6). Choose up to three creatures she can see within 10 ft. Each makes a DC 18 Constitution save, with disadvantage if Restrained by her Chain. A failure deals 49 (11d8) necrotic damage and gives one level of void taint, or one level of Exhaustion if substituting. A success halves the damage and avoids the added level. Kel Belleth regains HP equal to half the total necrotic damage dealt.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Blasphemous Word. When an attacker she can see hits her, Kel Belleth can speak a word of Void Speech. An attacker that hears her takes 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. She must be able to speak.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines:
Kel Belleth has three legendary actions and recovers them at the start of her turn. Use at most one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Teleport. Move magically up to 90 ft. to an unoccupied space she can see, bringing anything she is wearing or carrying.
Dark Litany (2 actions). Choose up to two creatures she can see within 60 ft. Each that hears her makes a DC 18 Wisdom save, with disadvantage if it has void taint or the substituted Exhaustion. Every saving target falls Prone. A failed save also Incapacitates it until the end of its next turn.
Ravenous Heart (2 actions). Use Soul Siphon if ready.

gm.title: Lair Actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, after tied turns, choose one effect. The same effect cannot be used in consecutive rounds.
Clawing Shadows. Until the next count 20, each hostile creature that starts its turn in dim light or darkness within 120 ft. of Kel Belleth makes a DC 18 Dexterity save. Failure deals 7 (2d6) necrotic damage and halves its speed until the start of its next turn.
Vile Chorus. Pick a point she can see within 120 ft. Each hostile creature within 30 ft. of that point makes a DC 18 Constitution save. Failure deals 7 (2d6) psychic damage and makes it vulnerable to necrotic damage until the next count 20.
Weeping Stone. All solid surfaces within 300 ft. of Kel Belleth become difficult terrain until the next count 20.

gm.title: Regional Effects
lines:
Gnawing Emptiness. Food and drink consumed in Sun Hollow turn to ash and do not count against starvation or dehydration.
Heavenly Hostility. Celestials other than Kel Belleth and void angels make a DC 18 Charisma save each hour spent in Sun Hollow. Failure adds one level of Exhaustion, bypassing the immunity granted by Angelic Resilience.
Oppressive Gray. Effects that create sunlight give bright light instead. Effects that ordinarily create bright light give dim light.
These effects fade 1d10 days after Kel Belleth dies.

gm.title: Encounter reference
lines: See Chapter 7, pp. 227–229 for the optional void taint rules. Soul Siphon specifies Exhaustion as the fallback.

gm.title: Statistics
lines: Speed · 30 ft., climb 30 ft., swim 30 ft.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: An amphibious frogfolk larva with a finned tail, dark round eyes and small webbed feet.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Damage immunity poison. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 9. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Acid Burst. When the tadpole drops to 0 HP, it bursts and deals 1 acid damage to every creature within 5 ft.
Amphibious. It breathes air and water.
Minion. An attack or a failed save that deals damage immediately drops the tadpole to 0 HP. Any other single instance of damage kills it if it deals at least 6 damage. The tadpole ignores lower damage from such an effect.
Noxious Skin. A creature that starts its turn within 5 ft. of at least three tadpoles makes a Constitution save with DC 10 plus the number of tadpoles within 5 ft. of it. Failure leaves it Poisoned until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite (Group Attack). Melee weapon attack +3, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1 piercing damage.

gm.title: Minion rules
lines:
Group attack. Two to five tadpoles that share a turn and can all reach a target spend their actions on one Bite roll. Add their number to +3. A hit deals 1 piercing damage per participant. A solo tadpole rolls at +3. Apply advantage or disadvantage only when it applies to all participants. Roll separately for groups with different cover or concealment. If the attack triggers an effect that can affect only one attacker, the target chooses which tadpole it affects.
Group opportunity attack. Multiple tadpoles can each spend their reaction to join the same Bite if the target provokes from them at the same time. Tadpoles have no Hit Dice and cannot score critical hits.
Overkill. A weapon hit dealing more than 6 damage leaves a surplus equal to damage minus 6. Reduce one additional eligible tadpole to 0 HP per 6 surplus damage or fraction of 6. Additional melee targets must be within reach. Additional ranged targets must be on the line from attacker through the first target and within the weapon’s short range. Opportunity attacks cannot deal overkill damage.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Bite uses the default 5-ft. reach for a melee attack.

lines: Speed · 25 ft., climb 20 ft., swim 30 ft.

gm.title: Hit point rule
lines: 7 × the yegg’s level in hit points. It has one d8 Hit Die per level.

lines: A small frogfolk retainer wearing light leather armor and carrying a poison knife and an acid flask.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Light armor. Saving throws +PB across all abilities. Skills Acrobatics +3 + PB, Athletics +PB, Stealth +3 + PB, Survival +2 + PB. Poison resistance. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 12. Languages Angulotl and Common.

gm.title: Mentor scaling
lines: The yegg uses its mentor’s level and proficiency bonus (PB). It acts on its mentor’s initiative, immediately before or after the mentor as the player chooses. At 0 HP it follows the same rules as a player character, including death saves.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The yegg breathes air and water.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Signature Attack (Poison Knife). Melee or ranged weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 1d4 + PB piercing plus 7 (2d6) poison damage. Starting at level 7, the yegg can make two of these attacks when it takes the Attack action. It can use its signature attack for opportunity attacks.

gm.title: Retainer features
lines:
Level 3, Death from Above! (3/day). As a bonus action, jump up to walking speed without provoking opportunity attacks. If the yegg jumps over an enemy, it can make a signature attack against that enemy with advantage. A hit deals extra piercing damage equal to PB.
Level 5, Lay Low (3/day). After hitting a creature with a signature attack while hidden, the yegg can use its reaction to stay hidden.
Level 7, Excoriating Acid (3/day). As an action, throw a flask at a visible point within 20 ft. Every creature within 10 ft. of the point makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB, taking PBd10 acid damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Description
lines: An invisible spirit feeds on a ward’s fear, jealousy, or anger. It takes over an object the ward cares about and uses it to keep others away.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Undead acquired template for a nonmagical object

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Physical attacks use the inhabited object’s attacks, damage, and special attacks. A bodiless animator makes no physical attacks.
Spell-like abilities (caster level 9). At will: animate objects, crushing despair (DC 16), fear (DC 16), rage (DC 15), scare (DC 14), and telekinesis.
Powerful Charge (Ex). In samples with this ability, add 4 damage to a charge. The host needs its own means of movement, such as wheels or legs, or must be propelled by telekinesis.
Blindsight (Ex). In samples with this ability, detect foes within 120 ft. Beyond that range, treat the animator as blinded.

gm.title: Template
lines: Animate a nonmagical base object using the animated object rules and change its type to Undead. Change its Hit Dice to d12s. Keep its speed, attacks, damage, saves, special attacks, qualities, and hardness. Add +2 deflection AC. Increase Strength by 2, with size adjustments as appropriate. Typical mental scores are Int 15, Wis 12, Cha 12. Base skills are Bluff +10, Hide +5, Intimidate +10, Listen +5, Search +7, Sense Motive +10, Spot +5. Apply size and Dexterity to Hide, and adjust skills for size and level as needed. Add Improved Initiative and Iron Will, plus Power Attack for more powerful animators.

gm.title: Ward and weaknesses
lines:
Ward (Su). An animator feeds on negative emotions produced by its ward and need not follow the ward’s orders. At more than 60 ft. from the ward, or when the ward goes more than a day without these emotions, it loses 1 Cha per day. Normal recovery resumes after rejoining its ward or finding another.
Outside an object it is naturally invisible and incorporeal. Invisibility purge does not cancel the natural invisibility. It cannot possess a magical object or an object under a spell. A successful melee touch with dispel evil expels it. Neither expulsion nor ordinary destruction of the host harms it. Soul bind or trap the soul can imprison it indefinitely. Turn or rebuke it as an 8 HD undead. To destroy it, trap it magically in the object, such as in an antimagic field, then destroy the object while it remains trapped.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A giant burrowing insect with a ridged exoskeleton, curved mandibles and long crooked feelers.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Athletics +6. Acid resistance. Immune to Flanked. Darkvision 60 ft., tremorsense 30 ft. Passive Perception 11. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Disoriented Resistance (2/day). On a failed save, the ankheg can succeed instead. It then cannot take bonus actions until the end of its next turn.
Earth Walk. Difficult terrain made of earth or stone costs no extra movement.
Soft Underbelly. A Prone creature attacking from within 5 ft. of the ankheg gets advantage in place of the usual disadvantage for attacking while Prone.
Unstable Tunneler. The ankheg leaves a tunnel 10 ft. across as it burrows. Each section collapses 1 minute after it leaves that space.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. A Large or smaller target is Grappled, escape DC 14. It is also Restrained while this grapple lasts, and the ankheg cannot Bite another target during it.
Claw. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Acid Spit (Recharge 6). Every creature in a 30-ft. line, 5 ft. wide, makes a DC 13 Dexterity save. On a failure the creature takes 7 (2d6) acid damage and is coated in acid. On a success it takes half damage only. A coated creature takes 3 (1d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Any creature can use an action to wipe acid off itself or another creature it can reach.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Earth Eruption. When it is burrowing within 10 ft. of the surface, the ankheg can rise without spending movement into a 10-ft. square directly above it. The square becomes difficult terrain. Each creature on the ground in it makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, the ankheg pushes it 5 ft. into an unoccupied space of the ankheg’s choice and rubble Restrains it. A creature can use an action to free itself or another creature within reach. On a success, the creature moves 5 ft. into an unoccupied space of its own choice.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Skitter. When a creature attacks the ankheg, it can move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Each can be used once per encounter after an enemy’s turn. The ankheg can use them in any order, at most one per round.
Big Bug! Every enemy within 30 ft. that can see the ankheg makes a DC 13 Wisdom save or is Frightened of it for 1 minute. The enemy repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the fear on a success.
Quick Burrow. If the ankheg is Grappled, end that condition for it. It burrows up to twice its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Grappling a Large or smaller creature does not halve its speed during this move.
Acid Bath. Each creature within 15 ft. makes a DC 13 Dexterity save, taking 7 (2d6) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.

Archmages are powerful (and usually quite old) spellcasters dedicated to the study of the arcane arts. Benevolent ones counsel kings and queens, while evil ones rule as tyrants and pursue lichdom. An archmage typically has one or more apprentice mages, and an archmage’s abode has numerous magical wards and guardians to discourage interlopers.

Fuel for the Fire. Plant life does not slow its movement as difficult terrain. If it starts a turn occupying plants that provide cover, it burns away the plants in its occupied spaces and regains 1d4 HP per 5-ft. square consumed. Regaining at least 17 HP this way recharges Magma Throw.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Molten Fist attacks.
Molten Fist. Melee weapon attack +9, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit for 16 (2d10 + 5) fire damage.
Stomp. Melee weapon attack +9, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 20 (3d10 + 5) fire damage. The target falls Prone on a failed DC 17 Constitution save.
Magma Throw (Recharge 5–6). Choose a point within 60 ft. Each creature within 15 ft. of that point makes a DC 17 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines:
The aspect has three legendary actions and recovers spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Detect. Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Molten Fist. Make one Molten Fist attack.
Magma Barrage (costs 2 actions). Use Magma Throw. Table ruling. If Magma Throw has yet to recharge, the aspect can take 17 cold damage to use it anyway.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Appendix A, Bestiary, p. 179. Scorched Grove finale, p. 173.

gm.title: Encounter notes
lines: Scorched Grove finale. Only the southern tree cover can fuel the aspect in this scene. It gains Rekindle and regains 10 HP if it starts its turn at 0 HP. Cold damage that drops it to 0 HP or hits it while at 0 prevents Rekindle on that turn and petrifies it when the turn starts. Petrification lasts an hour. It then returns to full HP. A shattered petrified aspect reassembles in 1d4 rounds, and any pieces still separated when petrification ends have Molten Skin.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The v1.04 Magma Barrage text is ambiguous about its 17 cold damage clause. Fuel for the Fire separately recharges Magma Throw after the aspect heals at least 17 HP from plants.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any terrain and activity cycle. Very rare. Solitary, appearing alone. No diet or treasure. Neutral, or matches the bearer. Intelligence High (13–14). Size Medium, 4 ft. long. Morale Champion (15–16). Magic resistance 25%.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Horns. In natural form, make one attack for 1d6 damage. With a running start, charge for 2d6 instead. A charge hit allows a separate trample attack for 2d4 damage. A target hit by the trample loses its initiative that round if it has yet to attack.
Humanoid weapons. Fight as a 7th-level warrior with +2 damage. The servant arrives with a halberd or can use a halberd, battle axe, or lance supplied by its bearer, including a magical one. It retains the weapon held when it shifted to natural form for its next humanoid transformation.

gm.title: Traits

gm.title: Bearer benefits
lines: While telepathically linked, the bearer gains +2 damage with halberds, battle axes, and lances. Baron Calturix of Nemausa is the known bearer.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Description
lines: A rock gnome builds an autognome in its own likeness, with painted features on a metal shell. Magic gives the machine a mind of its own, and a design flaw can leave it wandering Wildspace without orders.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Malfunction. If the autognome survives taking at least 15 damage from one source, roll a d20.
1–10. It keeps working.
11–12. It is incapacitated for 1 minute.
13–14. An arm drops off. It can make one fewer Shock attack until a creature uses an action to put that arm back on.
15–16. Its head falls off and switches off. It is blinded and deafened until a creature spends an action reattaching and reactivating its head.
17–20. The autognome explodes and is destroyed. Each creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 11 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) slashing damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
Unusual Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Shock attacks, subject to Malfunction.
Shock. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 7 (2d6) lightning damage.

gm.title: Orders
lines: A working autognome follows its maker's orders. Most protect themselves if attacked, defend gnomes against non-gnome attackers, and protect children regardless of species. An autognome might step between a Lunar Dragon Wyrmling and the adults fighting it.

lines: Nidhogg sends this wingless dragon of roots and clay in his place when a favored cultist needs his aid.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 23. Stealth 18. Immune to necrotic damage. Darkvision 120 ft. Keensense 60 ft. Speaks Common, Draconic, and Void Speech.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: STR +13 · DEX +2 · CON +11 · INT +5 · WIS +13 · CHA +10

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Aura of Hopelessness. A hostile creature that begins its turn within 15 ft. makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. On a failure, until its next turn starts, it rolls attacks with disadvantage and gains half as many HP from healing effects. The avatar can exempt any creature without spending an action.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The avatar can turn its failed save into a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Bite attacks, substituting a Tail attack for any of them.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 16 (2d8 + 7) piercing and 18 (4d8) necrotic damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d6 + 7) bludgeoning and 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. A Large or smaller target is Grappled (escape DC 19) and stays Restrained until the grapple ends. The avatar can hold up to four Medium or smaller creatures or two Large creatures.
Decaying Breath (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make a DC 19 Constitution save, taking 54 (12d8) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. Plant creatures and magical plants make this save with disadvantage. Use the maximum damage roll against them. Ordinary nonmagical plants in the cone die.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines:
The avatar has three legendary actions per round. It chooses one option at the end of another creature’s turn and refreshes its pool at the start of its own.
Detect. Pinpoint every creature and trap within 30 ft. automatically.
Move. Move up to half speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Void Wave (2 actions). Each creature within 15 ft. makes a DC 19 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 18 (4d8) necrotic damage and falls Prone. Void taint imposes disadvantage on the save. If a tainted creature fails, it takes another 4 (1d8) necrotic damage per level of void taint. The avatar heals HP equal to that extra damage, then the creature loses all levels of void taint.

gm.title: Encounter reference
lines: Void taint measures exposure to the Void. Use the target’s current levels for Void Wave. See Chapter 7 for the optional taint rules.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A bearded mercenary captain in half plate and a fur-lined cloak. His magic longsword, Nine Lives, has bloodstones set in its pommel.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Half plate. Saves Str +7, Con +7. Athletics +10, Deception +6, Insight +5, Intimidation +9, Perception +5. Passive Perception 15. Common.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Bloodstones (3 uses). When Uthrak fails a save while holding Nine Lives, he can succeed instead. If he does, he takes 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.
Exploit Opening (3/day). When Uthrak makes an attack, he can roll it with advantage.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks in any combination of Nine Lives and Whip.
Nine Lives. Melee weapon attack +8, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (1d8 + 5) slashing plus 3 (1d6) necrotic damage.
Whip. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d4 + 4) slashing damage. On a failed DC 15 Strength save, the target is pulled up to 15 ft. toward Uthrak.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Kneel, Peasant! A Large or smaller creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 15 Strength save. On a failure it takes 6 (1d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage and falls Prone.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Riposte. When a creature Uthrak can see misses him with a melee attack, he makes a melee attack against that creature.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Use each once per encounter, in any order after an enemy’s turn. Use at most one per round.
Shoot! Each ally within 60 ft. who can hear Uthrak can make a ranged weapon attack without spending an action.
Form Up! Uthrak and each ally within 60 ft. who can hear him can move up to their speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Each enters a defensive stance that ends when that creature moves again or becomes Restrained or Incapacitated. When at least two allies in the stance are within 5 ft. of one another, attack rolls against them have disadvantage.
Lead from the Front. Uthrak moves up to twice his speed without provoking opportunity attacks. During or after this move he can make up to four attacks with advantage, choosing Nine Lives or Whip for each and using a different target each time. After each attack, each ally within 5 ft. of that target can make a melee attack with advantage against the same target without spending an action.

gm.title: Encounter uses
lines: Uthrak lost his title after backing a failed rebellion. He now leads a mercenary band. Place melee guards close enough to form a line and ranged allies within earshot so his commands have targets.

gm.title: Hit point rule
lines: 7 + 7 × the caregiver’s level in hit points, with one d8 Hit Die per caregiver level.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A low-slung, eight-legged reptile with rough slate-green scales and watchful eyes.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor 15 + PB. Constitution save +2 + PB. Athletics +3 + PB and Survival +1 + PB. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11.

gm.title: Caregiver scaling
lines: PB is the caregiver’s proficiency bonus.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Signature Attack (Bite). Melee weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1d6 + PB piercing damage.

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Poison Spittle (2 Ferocity). Make a signature attack. On a hit, add damage equal to PB. A different creature of the basilisk’s choice within 5 ft. of the basilisk takes poison damage equal to PB.
Level 3, Poison Gaze (5 Ferocity). Choose up to three creatures the basilisk sees within 15 ft. Each makes a Constitution save against DC 10 + PB or becomes Poisoned until the start of the basilisk’s next turn.
Level 5, Lesser Petrifying Eye Beams (8 Ferocity). Choose one visible creature within 30 ft. It makes a Constitution save against DC 10 + PB or becomes Restrained as it starts turning to stone. If it is still Restrained this way at the end of its turn, it repeats the save. A success ends the effect. A failure Petrifies it for 1 hour, or until Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, or a similar supernatural effect ends the condition.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Heavy Glare. When the caregiver’s attack hits a creature that can see the basilisk, the target makes a Constitution save against DC 10 + PB. On a failure, until the start of the target’s next turn, its speed drops by 10 ft. and it cannot make opportunity attacks.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Description
lines: A dream stalker hides among cast shadows until someone sleeps. It takes on a broad human shape and spreads dark tendrils over the sleeper's face as it feeds.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any land or underground. Solitary or pack of 2–5. Always chaotic evil. No treasure. Advancement 6–10 HD (Medium). No level adjustment. Understands its languages from life but cannot speak. It can communicate with any creature that has a language through a dream.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +3. AC +3 Dex and +3 deflection. Touch 16 and flat-footed 13, calculated from those bonuses. Base attack +2, grapple +2 as listed. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +1, Ref +4, Will +6.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +9, Hide +10 or +20 with multiple light sources, Intimidate +11, Listen +9, Sense Motive +8, Spot +12. Alertness (bonus), Blind-Fight, Skill Focus (Hide).

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Undead traits, incorporeal subtype, and +4 turn resistance.
Hide in Plain Sight (Ex). It takes on the shape of a shadow cast by a creature or object. An observer can use Spot to notice an extra shadow. The bastellus gains a +10 circumstance bonus to Hide in a room with more than one light source. A dream invasion reveals its actual form, ending this benefit.
Light Blindness. Sunlight or comparably intense light such as daylight blinds it. It tries to smother the light with darkness.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Incorporeal touch +5 melee. In the waking world the touch deals no damage. A creature hit must make a DC 17 Will save against insanity or suffer confusion for 1d4 rounds.
Darkness (Sp). Twice per day as a 5th-level sorcerer.
Sleep (Sp). Every living creature within 30 ft. must succeed on a DC 14 Will save or fall asleep, regardless of Hit Dice.
Dream Invasion (Su). Take on its actual form and touch a sleeping victim's forehead. Witnesses make a DC 15 Horror save. The sleeper makes a DC 18 Will save. Failure gives the bastellus control of the dream and the sleeper wakes with one negative level. On a success, the sleeper can fight back inside the dream. Both sides retain their normal abilities, and the sleeper also has their current gear, spells, and feats. Supplies and spells used in the dream remain available after waking. The bastellus's dream touch deals 1d6 Wisdom damage instead of causing insanity. At Wisdom 0, the sleeper loses and wakes with one negative level. If the sleeper wins, they wake at once and recover lost Wisdom. The bastellus is stunned for 10 minutes per level of the sleeper.
Create Spawn (Su). Someone who dies from a dream invasion returns as an independent bastellus after 1d4 days, without their former abilities.

gm.title: Tactics
lines: It attacks the weakest or least guarded target, puts guards to sleep when needed, and flees when it can if cornered.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The attack header lists Constitution drain, but the detailed rules supply no amount or trigger. Use the detailed insanity and dream invasion rules. The printed grapple bonus is retained, though standard incorporeal creatures cannot physically grapple corporeal opponents.
The book gives no duration or daily limit for Sleep. For a runnable table default, use five minutes, as for the 3.5 spell at 5th caster level, with the printed save, radius, and unlimited HD.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

lines: Devil’s Sight. Magical darkness doesn’t impede the devil’s darkvision. Magic Resistance. The devil has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. Steadfast. The devil can’t be frightened while it can see an allied creature within 30 feet of it.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The devil makes two attacks: one with its beard and one with its glaive. Beard. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, the target can’t regain hit points. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Glaive. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage. If the target is a creature other than an undead or a construct, it must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or lose 5 (1d10) hit points at the start of each of its turns due to an infernal wound. Each time the devil hits the wounded target with this attack, the damage dealt by the wound increases by 5 (1d10). Any creature can take an action to stanch the wound with a successful DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) check. The wound also closes if the target receives magical healing.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Each makes a DC 15 Wisdom save or becomes frightened of the hag for 1 minute. While frightened this way, the creature is incapacitated, cannot read or understand others' speech, and can speak only gibberish. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. If it succeeds on a save or the effect ends, it is immune to this hag's Horrific Feast for 24 hours.

gm.title: Description
lines: A winter hag who rides a flying staff and uses blizzards to turn isolated settlements against one another.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Graystaff Magic. The hag can ride her graystaff as a Broom of Flying. Holding it lets her cast the staff spells under Innate Spellcasting. Only a bheur hag can use the staff. Replacing it after loss or destruction takes a year and a day.
Ice Walk. The hag can walk and climb on ice without ability checks. Ice and snow that count as difficult terrain cost her no additional movement.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d8 + 1) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) cold damage.
Maddening Feast. The hag feeds on the corpse of an enemy within 5 ft. that died in the past minute. Any creatures she chooses within 60 ft. that can see her must make a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, a creature is frightened of her for 1 minute. While frightened this way, it is incapacitated. It cannot read or understand speech and speaks only gibberish. The DM controls its erratic movement. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A successful save or the end of the effect makes the creature immune to this hag's Maddening Feast for 24 hours.

gm.title: Innate spellcasting
lines:
The hag uses Charisma (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks) and needs no material components.
At will. Ray of Frost.
1/day. Control Weather.
While holding the graystaff. Hold Person at will. Cone of Cold, Ice Storm, and Wall of Ice 3/day each.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
Optional lair actions for powerful hags. Grandmothers usually have three to five options. Aunties usually have at most one. On initiative count 20, after any creature tied with the hag, she can use one available option while in her lair and able to act. She cannot use the same option in consecutive rounds. If surprised, she must finish her first turn before she can use one. If an effect calls for a saving throw without giving a DC, use the DC of the hag's most powerful ability.
Pass Through Surfaces. The hag can pass through solid doors, walls, ceilings, and floors until initiative count 20 of the next round.
Doors and Windows. Open or close any number of visible doors and windows, choosing separately for each. A door closed this way can be magically locked. Forcing it open requires a DC 20 Strength check. The lock lasts until she unlocks the door or opens it with this lair action.
Blizzard. Center a cylinder 40 ft. tall and 20 ft. in radius on a point the hag can see within 120 ft. It lasts until initiative count 20 of the next round and lightly obscures creatures and objects in it. A creature that starts its turn there or enters for the first time on a turn is blinded until that same initiative count.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Pick regional effects for the hag's lair. A typical hag lair has three to five. Powerful hags and covens usually have more than a lone hag. If an effect calls for a save without giving a DC, use that of the hag's most powerful ability. When the hag dies or abandons the lair, effects can end immediately or fade within 2d10 days.
A grandmother's lair can produce any of the following within 1 mile. Appropriate small animals become unusually abundant. Beasts with Intelligence 2 or lower are charmed by the hag and act aggressively toward intruders at her direction. Carved figures, twig fetishes, or rag dolls appear in trees.
A powerful bheur hag can add any of the following within 1 mile. Snow slides can block routes or bury creatures, leaving them restrained and holding their breath until dug out. Human-sized blocks of ice contain bodies that can break out as zombies or release specters. Blizzards strike once every 2d12 hours and last 1d3 hours, halving overland speed and reducing normal visibility to 30 ft. Routes can loop back on themselves, making navigation difficult.

gm.title: Shared coven spellcasting
lines:
All three members must be within 30 ft. of one another to cast these spells. They draw from a single pool of slots, so one hag's casting spends a slot for the whole coven. Each counts as a 12th-level spellcaster for these wizard spells and uses Intelligence (save DC 13, +5 to hit).
Level 1 (4 shared slots). Identify, Ray Of Sickness.
Level 2 (3 shared slots). Hold Person, Locate Object.
Level 3 (3 shared slots). Bestow Curse, Counterspell, Lightning Bolt.
Level 4 (3 shared slots). Phantasmal Killer, Polymorph.
Level 5 (2 shared slots). Contact Other Plane, Scrying.
Level 6 (1 shared slot). Eyebite.

gm.title: Hag Eye mechanics
lines: A coven can keep one Hag Eye at a time. It has AC 10, 1 hit point, and darkvision 60 ft. Any member on the same plane as the eye can use an action to see through it. If the eye is destroyed, each member takes 3d10 psychic damage and is blinded for 24 hours. Making one takes an hour with all three hags present. None can be blinded. If any takes another action during the ritual, they must start over.

gm.title: Description
lines: A winter hag who rides a flying staff and uses blizzards to turn isolated settlements against one another.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Graystaff Magic. The hag can ride her graystaff as a Broom of Flying. Holding it lets her cast the staff spells under Innate Spellcasting. Only a bheur hag can use the staff. Replacing it after loss or destruction takes a year and a day.
Ice Walk. The hag can walk and climb on ice without ability checks. Ice and snow that count as difficult terrain cost her no additional movement.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d8 + 1) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) cold damage.
Maddening Feast. The hag feeds on the corpse of an enemy within 5 ft. that died in the past minute. Any creatures she chooses within 60 ft. that can see her must make a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, a creature is frightened of her for 1 minute. While frightened this way, it is incapacitated. It cannot read or understand speech and speaks only gibberish. The DM controls its erratic movement. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A successful save or the end of the effect makes the creature immune to this hag's Maddening Feast for 24 hours.

gm.title: Innate spellcasting
lines:
The hag uses Charisma (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks) and needs no material components.
At will. Ray of Frost.
1/day. Control Weather.
While holding the graystaff. Hold Person at will. Cone of Cold, Ice Storm, and Wall of Ice 3/day each.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
Optional lair actions for powerful hags. Grandmothers usually have three to five options. Aunties usually have at most one. On initiative count 20, after any creature tied with the hag, she can use one available option while in her lair and able to act. She cannot use the same option in consecutive rounds. If surprised, she must finish her first turn before she can use one. If an effect calls for a saving throw without giving a DC, use the DC of the hag's most powerful ability.
Pass Through Surfaces. The hag can pass through solid doors, walls, ceilings, and floors until initiative count 20 of the next round.
Doors and Windows. Open or close any number of visible doors and windows, choosing separately for each. A door closed this way can be magically locked. Forcing it open requires a DC 20 Strength check. The lock lasts until she unlocks the door or opens it with this lair action.
Blizzard. Center a cylinder 40 ft. tall and 20 ft. in radius on a point the hag can see within 120 ft. It lasts until initiative count 20 of the next round and lightly obscures creatures and objects in it. A creature that starts its turn there or enters for the first time on a turn is blinded until that same initiative count.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Pick regional effects for the hag's lair. A typical hag lair has three to five. Powerful hags and covens usually have more than a lone hag. If an effect calls for a save without giving a DC, use that of the hag's most powerful ability. When the hag dies or abandons the lair, effects can end immediately or fade within 2d10 days.
A grandmother's lair can produce any of the following within 1 mile. Appropriate small animals become unusually abundant. Beasts with Intelligence 2 or lower are charmed by the hag and act aggressively toward intruders at her direction. Carved figures, twig fetishes, or rag dolls appear in trees.
A powerful bheur hag can add any of the following within 1 mile. Snow slides can block routes or bury creatures, leaving them restrained and holding their breath until dug out. Human-sized blocks of ice contain bodies that can break out as zombies or release specters. Blizzards strike once every 2d12 hours and last 1d3 hours, halving overland speed and reducing normal visibility to 30 ft. Routes can loop back on themselves, making navigation difficult.

gm.title: Shared coven spellcasting
lines:
All three members must be within 30 ft. of one another to cast these spells. They draw from a single pool of slots, so one hag's casting spends a slot for the whole coven. Each counts as a 12th-level spellcaster for these wizard spells and uses Intelligence (save DC 13, +5 to hit).
Level 1 (4 shared slots). False Life, Inflict Wounds.
Level 2 (3 shared slots). Gentle Repose, Ray Of Enfeeblement.
Level 3 (3 shared slots). Animate Dead, Revivify, Speak With Dead.
Level 4 (3 shared slots). Blight, Death Ward.
Level 5 (2 shared slots). Contagion, Raise Dead.
Level 6 (1 shared slot). Circle Of Death.

gm.title: Hag Eye mechanics
lines: A coven can keep one Hag Eye at a time. It has AC 10, 1 hit point, and darkvision 60 ft. Any member on the same plane as the eye can use an action to see through it. If the eye is destroyed, each member takes 3d10 psychic damage and is blinded for 24 hours. Making one takes an hour with all three hags present. None can be blinded. If any takes another action during the ritual, they must start over.

lines: The Queen of Thieves brings her arena champion out of its den with a whistle.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception +4. Immune to acid. Blindsight 30 ft., passive Perception 14. No languages.

gm.title: Base stat block
lines: Tyrannosaurus Rex, SRD 5.1 (2014 fifth-edition rules). The arena encounter adds Acid Spew, acid immunity, blindsight, and the Queen’s charm. Use the adventure’s CR 9.

gm.title: Traits
lines: The Queen’s Charm. Big Linda is permanently Charmed by the Queen of Thieves and generally obeys her spoken commands.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Tail attack against different targets.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 33 (4d12 + 7) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller target is Grappled (escape DC 17) and Restrained until the grapple ends. Big Linda cannot Bite a different target during that grapple.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
Acid Spew (recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make a DC 15 Dexterity save against 49 (11d8) acid damage, halved on success.

gm.title: Encounter notes
lines: In Buckledown Row, the Queen of Thieves can call Big Linda out of her den by whistling.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: An amorphous predator that can imitate a building or a stone doorway, opening into a tooth-lined maw.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Deception +2, Stealth +5. Immune to acid damage and bludgeoning damage from falling. Immune to Prone. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
False Appearance (object form). A motionless mimic passes for an ordinary object.
Mimicry. The mimic can imitate sounds it has heard, including voices. A listener can recognize the imitation with a DC 12 Wisdom (Insight) check.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) acid damage. A Large or smaller creature hit this way is Grappled (escape DC 15).
Gnashing Maw. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing plus 10 (3d6) acid damage. If the mimic is grappling the target, deal an extra 3 (1d6) acid damage.
Shapechanger. The mimic can become any object of Medium size or larger or return to its true amorphous form. Its size is the only statistic that changes. Worn or carried gear keeps its shape. On death the mimic resumes its true form.
Envelop. While grappling a creature, the mimic uses Shapechanger to become an object at least as large as that creature if it is not already in such a form. The creature is then enveloped and its grapple ends. It cannot breathe, is Blinded and Restrained, and has total cover from attacks and effects outside the mimic. It moves with the mimic and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the mimic’s turns.
The mimic can envelop one creature at a time. An engulfed creature can spend an action to make a DC 15 Strength check, escaping into an empty space of its choice within 5 ft. of the mimic on a success. It also escapes automatically if the mimic uses Shapechanger or Panic Shift, becomes Incapacitated, or dies.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Panic Shift (1/day). When it takes damage, the mimic releases any Grappled or enveloped creatures and becomes a Small, dense, spiked object. In this form its walking and climbing speeds double, it resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from mundane attacks, and its actions are limited to Dash, Disengage, and Shapechanger. A creature within 5 ft. that touches it or hits it with a melee attack takes 10 (3d6) piercing damage. This ends when the mimic dies or uses Shapechanger to take another form.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The variant keeps the base block’s true-form size and printed physical damage. Its listed changes add acid damage to both attacks and allow it to assume larger object forms.

gm.title: Description
lines: A black swan with a gold bill. In humanoid form it looks like an elven woman in a feathered cloak.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any terrain and activity cycle. Very rare. Solitary, appearing alone. No diet or treasure. Neutral, or matches the bearer. Intelligence Exceptional (15–16). Size Medium, 5 ft. tall. Morale Champion (15–16). Magic resistance 40%.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Beak. Make one attack for 1d6 in natural form. The humanoid form carries a dagger.
Charm. Choose a target at will, once per target per day. Immortals are immune. The target saves vs. breath weapon with +1 for each 10% of magic resistance or fraction thereof. Total charm immunity grants +10 instead. A natural 1 fails regardless of modifiers. On failure, the target cannot harm the swan or its bearer.
Mental command. Use the 1st-level priest spell on a creature already charmed. A command that provokes a strong negative response allows a new save to break the charm.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Enchanted defense. A creature that resists the charm still needs a +1 or better weapon to hit the servant.
Both active forms can use charm and command.

gm.title: Bearer benefits
lines: While in contact with the servant, the bearer gains the protection against weapons below +1 and can use fly three times per day. The Count of Enom is the known bearer.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The profile gives no charm duration. Keep the charm and its stated escape save together when running the encounter.

gm.title: Description
lines: A paladin who terrifies nearby enemies and blinds or knocks down foes with a smite.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Glaive and Shortbow.
Glaive. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Dreadful Aspect (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Each enemy within 30 ft. makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is frightened of the blackguard for 1 minute. If it ends its turn more than 30 ft. from the blackguard, it can repeat the save, ending the effect on a success.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one of the following spells using Charisma (spell save DC 13).
2/day each. Command, Dispel Magic, Find Steed.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Smite. Immediately after the blackguard hits a target with an attack roll, it can force that target to make a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failed save, choose Blind or Shove.
Blind. The target is blinded for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Shove. Push the target up to 10 ft. away from the blackguard and knock it prone.

Medium elemental (Water, Mists). CR 3. 30 HP (4d8 + 12). Initiative +1. Speed 20 ft..
AC 19, touch 11, flat-footed 18. Base attack +3, grapple +6. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft.
Attack Slam +6 melee (1d8 + 4 plus Blood Drain). Full attack Slam +6 melee (1d8 + 4 plus Blood Drain).
Fort +7, Ref +2, Will +1. Str 16, Dex 12, Con 17, Int 5, Wis 11, Cha 11. Listen +7, Spot +7.
Feats include Power Attack. Advancement 5–7 HD, Medium.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Slam. Make one melee slam, or use the full-attack count in the chosen tier. Blood Drain applies to every successful slam against a living creature.
Blood Drain (Ex). After a slam hits a living creature, the elemental attempts to drain its blood as a free action. Fortitude DC equals its HD plus its Constitution modifier. Failure deals 1d4 Constitution damage. The elemental gains 1 HP for each point of Constitution damage actually dealt.
Drench (Ex). Touch extinguishes an exposed nonmagical flame at least one size category smaller than the elemental. Touching magical fire can dispel it as dispel magic at caster level equal to the elemental’s HD.
Engulf (Ex). The elemental can engulf a foe at least one size smaller in a round when it makes no slams. The target can make an attack of opportunity and forgo the save, or decline the attack and attempt a DC 16 Reflex save. An engulfed creature is subject to the 3.5 drowning rules. When an attack hits the elemental, split the damage evenly between it and the engulfed target on a 50% roll if the elemental is one size larger, or 10% if it is two sizes larger. With a gap of three or more categories, only the elemental takes damage.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Darkvision 60 ft. Immune to poison, sleep, paralysis, stunning, critical hits, and flanking. Does not eat, sleep, or breathe. It cannot be raised or resurrected, though limited wish, wish, miracle, or true resurrection can restore it. Drawn from blood or from water taken from drowned lungs. Exceptionally evil blood can increase its HD. It cannot enter or cross a large body of water. Forced contact with a body of water at least as large as itself deals 1d10 damage each round until it escapes.

gm.title: Drowning
lines: In 3.5, a creature can hold its breath for twice its Constitution score in rounds. Each standard or full-round action uses an additional round of that reserve. Once it runs out, make a DC 10 Constitution check each round, increasing the DC by 1 each round. On a failure it falls unconscious at 0 HP, drops to −1 HP in the following round, and dies in the third.

gm.title: Dread elemental rules
lines:
Printed source. Elemental, Dread, p. 63, and Mists subtype, pp. 7–8.
In Ravenloft, calling a standard elemental has a 20% chance of producing a dread elemental. Summoning magic always produces the dread form. Accidental dread elementals are uncontrolled, and the Dark Powers supply the matching materials. Intentional conjuring requires the matching material and uses the usual chance for the elemental to break control.
Dread elementals understand speech but do not communicate. Their Mists subtype makes them native throughout Ravenloft and allows them to be summoned in any domain. A dismissed dread elemental returns to Ravenloft itself, so the realm's restrictions on calling do not break the calling pact.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slap +2 melee (1d4 + 2).
Full Attack. Two slaps +2 melee (1d4 + 2 each). If both hit, the target is automatically grappled. Starting the next round, Constrict deals 2d4 + 2 each round. Pliability (Ex). It can squeeze through a gap at least 1 inch wide or fold into a 1-cubic-foot container, including an airtight one. Soak it at least once per week or keep it in a reservoir of water. If it dries out it loses its special maneuvers, including its grapple attack, and moves and fights as a zombie. A dried boneless takes double damage from fire.

gm.title: Creating a Boneless
lines:
Acquired template for a corporeal, formerly skeletal creature other than an undead, with fewer than 20 HD. Keep size. Replace type with undead and drop alignment and kind subtypes without adding the augmented subtype. Keep base statistics where the template gives no change. Drop class Hit Dice, to a minimum of 3 HD, and use d12s for current and future Hit Dice. Set speed to 30 ft. or 60 ft. on all fours. It cannot fly, even with wings.
Keep weapons and weapon proficiencies. Retain natural attacks except claws and bites. Each hand deals 1d4 + Strength bonus, and constriction after a successful grapple deals 2d4 + Strength bonus per round. Replace other special attacks with Constrict. Keep only extraordinary special qualities that enhance melee attacks and add the traits listed above.
Base saves are Fort and Ref +1 per 3 HD and Will +2 plus half HD. Dexterity increases by 2, Wisdom becomes 10, and Charisma becomes 1. Remove Constitution and Intelligence scores, skills, and prior feats. Gain Agility. CR starts at 3 and rises with HD. Advancement follows the base creature unless it advanced by class, in which case use none. Any environment or organization, no treasure or level adjustment, always evil and usually neutral evil.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The sample stat block and template use 2d4 + Strength for constriction. The general combat paragraph says 2d4. This summary uses the sample's explicit 2d4 + 2.
The sample lists Will +2. Its template's formula gives +3 at 3 HD. Use the listed sample save for this encounter and the template formula when creating another boneless.
