gm.title: Description
lines: A decrepit minotaur with a dented crown and a clay amphora wanders the Katachthon foothills. He claims Mogis cursed him after he chose his child as his heir, and now tests strangers for the right to succeed him.

gm.title: Starting hit points
lines: Antigonos uses the 2014 Minotaur and begins the encounter with 38 of its usual 76 HP. The listed Hit Dice and most other statistics come from the base creature.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Charge. After moving at least 10 ft. straight toward a target, hitting it with Gore on the same turn deals an extra 9 (2d8) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or be pushed up to 10 ft. away and knocked prone.
Labyrinthine Recall. Antigonos remembers every route he has traveled.
Reckless. At the start of his turn he can choose to gain advantage on melee weapon attack rolls that turn. If he does, attacks against him have advantage until the start of his next turn.
Decrepit State. Antigonos has disadvantage on his attack rolls.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d12 + 4) slashing damage.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Amphora. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. If the amphora is empty, the target is restrained inside. A restrained creature can use an action to make a DC 14 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, escaping on a success. Destroying the amphora also ends the restraint. The amphora has AC 8, 20 HP, and immunity to poison and psychic damage.

gm.title: Test of the Amphora
lines:
Antigonos invites a Medium creature to climb into the amphora while he steadies it. After the creature enters, roll a d20.
1–9. He judges the creature too small and pours dirt into the amphora. The creature makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, it is blinded and restrained and begins suffocating. On a success, apply the effects of a hit from his Amphora attack.
10–19. He judges the creature too large and attacks it with his greataxe.
20. He declares the creature his heir, gives it his crown, robes, and belt pouch, and leaves.

gm.title: Contending with Antigonos
lines: He leaves if no one agrees to his test. Insults and theft can provoke him, and in a fight he may switch to random targets with his greataxe or empty amphora. If the party refrains from attacking him, he calms after a few rounds. A character who urges him to turn away from Mogis can make a DC 14 Charisma (Persuasion) check. On a success, he abandons the amphora and leaves to learn about a new deity. On a failure, he still departs in thought. Award experience for overcoming him whether or not the party fights.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: This wandering geist appears where a tragedy like the one it helped cause is about to occur. Its mourning begins 1d6 days before disaster.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Printed 2nd-level human commoner example. Initiative +2. AC 12 (+2 Dex), touch 12, flat-footed 10. Base attack +1, grapple +1. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +0, Ref +2, Will +0. Hide +10, Listen +10, Profession +7, Search +8, Spot +11. Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Profession). No treasure. Any land or underground. Solitary. Any alignment.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
No physical attack.
Aura of Despair (Sp). Creatures within 120 ft. make a DC 10 Will save. On a failure they take a −2 morale penalty to saves, attack rolls, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls until they leave the aura. A success grants immunity to this geist’s aura for 24 hours.
Mind Games (Su). As a free action, project an image of itself to living creatures within 30 ft. Use major image as a phantasm. A DC 10 Will save prevents perception of the image. The sight may also call for a Horror save if its death was particularly gruesome.

gm.title: Traits

gm.title: Description
lines: These hungry dead return to the same isolated house night after night, retreating at sunrise and trying again after dark.

gm.title: Description
lines: A corpse-dwelling scavenger whose eight legs resemble exposed ribs. It uses the corpse for cover and to anchor its tendrils.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +3. AC 17 (+2 size, +3 Dex, +2 natural), touch 15, flat-footed 14. Base attack +0, grapple −12. Space 2 ft., reach 15 ft. Fort +4, Ref +3, Will +0. Hide +18, Spot +4. Underground. Solitary or clusters of 2–6. No treasure. Always neutral. Advancement 2–4 HD (Small), with overlapping ranges in print.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Tendrils (Ex). Tendril +5 ranged (1d2 plus pinning). Full attack, up to eight tendrils +5 ranged each (1d2 plus pinning per hit). On any hit, the target makes one Reflex save at DC 13 + the number of tendrils that hit or is pinned. The stalker itself is not considered grappled. Escape requires an Escape Artist or Strength check at DC 15 + the number of wrapping tendrils. Each tendril deals 1 damage per round to the bound target. An ally who uses Aid Another to help takes 1 damage. The stalker keeps attacking that target with tendrils that previously missed, at the printed +4 to hit. Each tendril has AC 20 (+8 size, +2 natural), 2 separate HP, and takes damage only from slashing weapons. Tendrils continue stinging for 1d4 rounds after the stalker dies.
Infest (Ex). Drag the pinned victim 5 ft. closer each round without provoking attacks of opportunity. When the victim reaches the stalker's square, release 2d4 larvae as a free action and die. If killed first, the stalker releases its larvae toward an adjacent creature. Larvae burrow on the following round. Before then, a helper who succeeds on a DC 15 Spot check can remove 1d4 larvae as a standard action. While larvae are burrowed, each deals 1d2 temporary Constitution damage per round unless the victim succeeds on a Fortitude save at DC 12 + the number of burrowed larvae. Removing each requires a DC 15 Heal check. Helpers risk the tendrils if the victim is still bound. Remove disease kills all larvae. They mature in two weeks.

gm.title: Senses
lines: Heatsense (Ex) detects warm-blooded creatures within 30 ft. through invisibility or concealment. Treat the stalker as blinded against creatures that give off no heat. Vermin traits.

gm.title: Tactics
lines: Stay hidden in a corpse until warm-blooded prey comes within 15 ft., then strike with the tendrils.

gm.title: Description
lines: A painted marionette that uses silver needles to disable a victim and take over their body.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +0. AC 14 (+4 size), touch 14, flat-footed 14. Base attack +0, grapple −12. Space 1 ft., reach 0 ft. Fort +0, Ref +0, Will −1. Climb +8, including a +8 racial bonus. Odiare. Solitary or packs of 2–8. No treasure. Always chaotic evil. Advancement 3–4 HD (Tiny).

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Straight razor −2 melee (1d4−2) or silver needle +0 ranged (special).
Silver Needles (Su). Carries 10 reusable needles. Throw one up to 15 ft. A hit strikes a limb the carrionette chooses and deals no damage. A failed DC 14 Will save paralyzes that limb and makes the trailing silver cord invisible. Removing the needle ends paralysis after 1d4 rounds. The needles are nonmagical, and carrionettes are immune to the paralysis.
Possession (Su). Drive a silver needle into the neck of a sleeping, unconscious, or fully immobilized humanoid or monstrous humanoid. The doll and victim swap essences indefinitely, as magic jar with no save. The carrionette wakes in the stolen body after one round and can safely remove its own needles. The victim wakes in the doll after one hour. The doll remains linked to the carrionette, which dies if the doll is destroyed. If the victim in the doll drives a silver needle into the stolen body, reverse the swap. The carrionette remains inert in the doll for an hour, and the victim wakes in their own body after one round.
Ventriloquism (Sp). At will.

gm.title: Defenses
lines: Construct traits and darkvision 60 ft. Warp wood instantly destroys the carrionette.

gm.title: Description
lines: A foot-tall lizard kin ambusher. Caymas use hidden village entrances and prefer a quick strike followed by retreat.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Temperate to subtropical swamps or forests. Uncommon. Village of 10d6 adults and half as many noncombatants. Active at any time. Omnivore. Intelligence 8–10. Treasure K. Neutral. No magic resistance. Height about 1 foot. Morale 8–10.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack once for 1d3 damage or use a weapon. Bone daggers deal 1d2. A bok deals 1d6. Caymas use it two-handed as a pike and cannot throw it.
Ambush. A concealed cayma imposes a −2 penalty on the target’s surprise roll.

gm.title: Senses and skills
lines: Infravision 90 feet. Hide in Shadows and Move Silently each succeed 40% of the time. Speaks a Shazak dialect. Knowing one lizard kin dialect gives basic comprehension of the other two. A few individuals speak Common.

gm.title: Village shaman
lines: Each village has a shaman equivalent to a 5th- to 7th-level priest. The shaman has AC 6 and raises a party’s morale by one level. XP by Hit Dice, with Legacy value second. 5 HD 420 or 650 XP. 6 HD 650 or 975 XP. 7 HD 975 or 1,400 XP.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: A cayma entering the cursed lands can acquire a Legacy and needs cinnabryl to prevent Affliction. A standard cayma with a Legacy is worth 120 XP.

gm.title: Cayma grenades
lines:
A Wokan can supply ceramic grenades. On impact against a hard surface, roll 1d20. The grenade breaks and releases its cloud on 1–17.
Sleep. Within 1 foot of the impact, anyone whose head or breathing organ is in the cloud must save vs. breath weapon or sleep for 1d4 turns.
Choke. Same area and save as sleep. Failure leaves the victim unable to attack or defend for 1d6 rounds.
Fog. A 5-foot radius blocks ordinary vision and infravision for 1d6 rounds. Strong wind halves the duration.
Weapon details. Savage Coast Campaign Book, Part 2, pp. 136–137.

gm.title: Description
lines: Owl-eyed celestial bounty hunters judge whether the punishment a petitioner seeks fits the injury. A celebrun that takes a contract pursues its quarry with immortal patience.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Studded leather. Perception 16, Stealth 17. Resistant to radiant damage and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Immune to Blinded. Darkvision 60 ft. Languages Celestial and Common. Telepathy 60 ft.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +3, Dex +7, Con +2, Int +1, Wis +6, Cha +3

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Celestial Resilience. Resistance to radiant damage and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attack.
Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks count as magical.
Seekers Sign. On hitting a creature with Talons or Golden Helm, the celebrun can mark it. It knows the target’s exact location whenever they share a plane. The mark ends when either dies or it marks a different creature.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Greatsword and one Talons attack, or two Golden Helm attacks.
Greatsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 14 Dexterity save or be Blinded until the end of its next turn.
Golden Helm. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d4 + 4) slashing plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage.
Whirling Wheel (recharge 5–6). Every creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. Failure deals 14 (4d6) slashing plus 18 (4d8) radiant damage. Success halves both.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Horn of Heaven. Choose a visible non-Celestial creature within 60 ft. that hears the horn. On a failed DC 14 Charisma save, golden light outlines it for 1 minute, negating the benefits of Invisible and granting advantage to attacks against it. Repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: This vampire drains a pinned victim’s mind and uses the same lunar powers as a nosferatu.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Adapted from the printed fledgling nosferatu. Initiative +8. Touch AC 14, flat-footed AC 22. BAB +3, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +6.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Choose slam +4 melee (1d6 + 1), +1 rapier +8 melee (1d6 + 2, 18–20), or masterwork heavy crossbow +8 ranged (1d10, 19–20/×2).
Domination (Su). Standard action on a target within 30 ft. that the vampire can look at. Will DC 18 or dominate person at caster level 12.
Intelligence Drain (Ex). Pin a living target in a grapple and drain 1d4 Intelligence each round the pin holds. At Intelligence 0 or less the victim becomes catatonic. Use this in place of Blood Drain. The source describes the persistent Domination save as a Blood Drain rider and gives no new rider for this replacement.
Children of the Night (Su, 1/day). Standard action to call 1d6 + 1 rat swarms, 1d4 + 1 bat swarms, or 3d6 wolves. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 10/silver and magic, cold and electricity resistance 10, turn resistance +4, spider climb, undead traits. Gaseous form as a standard action at will, with indefinite duration and fly speed 20 ft. (perfect). Alternate Form can assume bat, dire bat, wolf, or dire wolf form. As a standard action assume the listed animal form. Lose the slam and domination, gain the animal’s natural weapons and extraordinary attacks, and retain this form until the next sunrise or another change.
Lunar Regeneration. Direct moonlight converts past damage to nonlethal damage even after apparent death. Heal 3, 4, 6, or 8 per round in crescent, half, gibbous, or full moonlight, plus the age bonus. Fire, acid, and blessed or holy weapons deal normal damage. It can reattach severed limbs. It cannot regenerate a lost limb or recover nonlethal damage with its head detached.
Restful Sleep. While at 1 HP or more, heal 1 HP per HD per hour in its coffin. Daylight disables supernatural abilities. After exposure to direct sunlight, it must sleep in its coffin for 8 hours to restore them. Existing domination persists, and an alternate form cannot end until powers return.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: If a victim dies while its Intelligence is 0 or less from the drain, it rises under the creator’s control on the next full moon. A victim with 4 or fewer HD returns as spawn and one with 5 or more HD as a cerebral vampire. The creature regains its original Intelligence in undeath. Cerebral spawn also replace Blood Drain with Intelligence Drain. Nosferatu spawn retain charm, gaseous form, spider climb and daylight powerlessness. They heal 2 HP per hour asleep in their coffins if at 1 HP or more, or 2 HP per round in direct full moonlight.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines: Garlic repels it, and a clearly presented holy symbol or mirror keeps it 5 ft. away. It cannot enter a private home without invitation. A stake through the heart kills it while left in place. At 0 HP it collapses but may return in moonlight. Burn the whole body or scatter the severed limbs beyond its minions’ reach. Running water costs one-third of HP each round and destroys it after 3 rounds of immersion.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +21, Diplomacy +16, Gather Information +11, Hide +12, Intimidate +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +12, Search +13, Sense Motive +15, Spot +12. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Diplomacy), Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Encounter adaptation
lines: Apply the strain to the 3.5 vampire template. Retain unmodified abilities, size, BAB, saves and skill points. The base vampire uses undead d12 Hit Dice and has no Constitution score. Keep an existing swim speed and ignore vulnerability to immersion in running water if the base creature can swim. Use save DC 10 + half HD rounded down + Charisma modifier unless specified. Age rows replace one another. Nosferatu lack the base vampire’s Energy Drain. Age DR always requires silver and magic. The cerebral subtype changes the feeding attack only.

gm.title: Age modifiers
lines:
Apply one row to a base creature. The sample already includes its adjustments. Ability scores are listed in Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha order.
Fledgling. Abilities 4/4/2/2/6. Speed +0 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 10, lunar healing +0.
Mature. Abilities 4/4/4/2/8. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 15, lunar healing +0.
Old. Abilities 6/6/4/4/8. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +7, turn resistance +5, CR +3. DR 15, lunar healing +1.
Ancient. Abilities 6/6/6/4/10. Speed +20 ft., natural AC +7, turn resistance +6, CR +3. DR 20, lunar healing +1.
Eminent. Abilities 8/8/6/6/10. Speed +20 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +7, CR +4. DR 20, lunar healing +2.
Patriarch. Abilities 10/10/8/8/12. Speed +30 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +8, CR +5. DR 25, lunar healing +3.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The cerebral subtype has no separate stat block. The header and combat stats use the printed nosferatu sample with the explicit feeding substitution.

lines: An Arak construct made from a stolen mortal shadow. Its maker assigns it a single task, which it pursues to the exclusion of nearly everything else.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. One weapon attack at +2 for weapon damage. Noncombatants do not attack.
Powriekin. Favor poisoned daggers and darts. Sneak attack adds 2d6 as a 3rd-level rogue. Trained Hide and Move Silently with +10 racial bonuses.
Sheekin. Does not fight, even when attacked. Trained Perform with a +20 racial bonus.
Sithkin. Prefers a simple weapon such as a sickle. Can rebuke undead as a 7th-level evil cleric. Undead other than domain lords will not attack unless it attacks first. It never speaks and has a +10 racial bonus on Move Silently.
Tegkin. Uses simple weapons or shortbow or longbow. Trained Survival +10 racial, Hide, Move Silently and Spot +4 racial.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Construct traits and darkvision 60 ft. Initiative +0, BAB/grapple +0/+0, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +1, Ref +1, Will +1. It knows its former owner's languages and dissolves into shadow when killed. Racial skills count as trained despite having no skill points. Shadow Rift, solitary or pack of 2–12, no treasure. Its alignment follows its maker.

gm.title: Running the encounter
lines: An Arak puts a mortal to sleep with faerie food and lights a magic candle. Over its five-hour burn the mortal cannot wake unless it is extinguished. The Arak uses black dust and a silver sickle to remove the shadow, then must deliver it to the Shadow Rift before the candle goes out. Success creates the changeling and leaves the mortal as an Intelligence-less, shadowless automaton that refuses to defend itself. Wish or miracle restores the mortal. Resurrection cast on the living changeling destroys it and restores the mortal.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: CR is 0 for a noncombatant and 1 for a combatant. The entry prints no separate touch or flat-footed AC, innate poison profile, or poison DC.

lines: Appendix B, p. 219. Purge Contamination, Appendix D, p. 229.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Devotion. Advantage on saves against being Charmed or Frightened.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
9th-level cleric spellcasting. Wisdom, printed save DC 12, printed +4 to hit.
At will. Light, Mending, Sacred Flame, Spare the Dying.
1st level (4 slots). Bless, Guiding Bolt, Healing Word.
2nd level (3 slots). Lesser Restoration, Prayer of Healing, Spiritual Weapon.

gm.title: Setting spell
lines: Purge Contamination (3rd level). Cast for 1 hour and touch one contaminated humanoid. Consume 100 gp of alchemical fluids or holy water. Remove every contamination level and mutation, then give the target one level of Exhaustion for each level removed.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) on a two-handed melee attack.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

lines: The printing explicitly lists spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spells, and +3 to hit with the spear. The profile retains those values.

gm.title: Description
lines: This fledgling was a human monk. It can levitate toward a target, paralyze them with a look, or vanish before approaching.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Fledgling sample, 5th-level human monk. Initiative +8. AC components +4 Dex, +3 Wis, +1 monk, +6 natural, +1 armor. Touch 18, flat-footed 17. Base attack +5, grapple +10. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +4, Ref +10, Will +7.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +10 melee for 1d4 + 5 and energy drain, +1 kama +13 melee for 1d6 + 6, or masterwork sling +8 ranged for 1d4.
Full attack. Two of the listed claws, one listed kama attack, or one listed sling attack.
Mesmerism (Su). Standard action against one target within 30 ft. who meets its eyes. Will DC 17 or hold monster at caster level 12.
Energy Drain (Su). Claw hits bestow one negative level on a living target.
Blood Drain (Ex). Pin a living creature in a grapple. Each round the pin is maintained, drain 1d4 Constitution and gain 5 temporary HP.
Spell-like abilities. At will, insect plague and passwall at caster level 12. DC 17 if a save applies.
Children of the Night (Su). Once per day as a standard action, call 4d8 cats or 2d6 panthers using leopard statistics. They arrive after 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 10/bamboo and magic. Cold and electricity resistance 10. Turn resistance +4. Undead traits. The sample retains evasion, slow fall, stunning attack, and unarmed strike from monk. At 5th monk level, slow fall reduces the effective distance by 20 ft. when a wall is within reach.
Corrosion (Su). A nonmagical weapon that hits must make a DC 14 Fortitude save or take 2d8 acid damage, ignoring hardness.
Invisibility (Su). At will as a standard action, become invisible indefinitely until it makes a direct attack.
Weightless Step (Su). Levitate at will as a free action at caster level 12. The fledgling can also move horizontally up to 10 ft. in this state.
Alternate Form (Su). Assume tiger form as a standard action. It remains in that form until it changes again or until sunrise. Apply the ordinary vampire form rules to its native attacks and the tiger’s extraordinary attacks.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: A humanoid or monstrous humanoid killed by energy drain rises as vampire spawn 1d4 days after burial. One reduced to Constitution 0 by blood drain returns as spawn if it had 4 or fewer HD or as a chiang-shi if it had 5 or more. A creator controls its spawn until it dies.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines:
It avoids smoke made by burning rosemary and myrrh and cannot touch a creature wearing a rosemary and ivy garland. It cannot cross running water on its own. It can be carried over in a coffin or on a conveyance. It rests by day in a coffin lined with native soil. Scattering rosemary and myrrh on that soil bars it permanently from that coffin.
Direct sunlight leaves it with a single move or attack action. It is destroyed in the next round if it cannot escape the light. Immersion in running water takes away one-third of its HP each round and destroys it at the end of round 3. A vampire strain whose base creature has a swim speed retains it and escapes the immersion weakness.
At 1 HP or more it heals 5 HP per round. At 0 HP or less it turns invisible and intangible and flees without attacking. It is destroyed if it misses the 2-hour deadline to reach its coffin. After 1 hour there it reaches 1 HP and resumes healing.
A bamboo shaft through the heart kills it while the shaft remains in place. For permanent destruction, bless a rosemary blossom, put it in the vampire’s mouth, then sew its lips and eyes shut with a silver needle and golden thread.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Balance +12, Bluff +10, Concentration +10, Diplomacy +10, Hide +12, Jump +13, Listen +13, Move Silently +12, Search +9, Sense Motive +11, Spot +13, Tumble +12. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Deflect Arrows, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Weapon Focus with kama.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any environment, especially Rokushima Táiyoo. Solitary, pair, or gang of 2–5. An organized group can contain 1–2 full vampires and 2–5 vampire spawn. Speaks languages known in life. Always evil. Double standard treasure. The printed monk has a +1 kama, bracers of armor +1, and two potions of cat’s grace.

gm.title: Template and age
lines: Apply the strain to a humanoid or monstrous humanoid using the 3.5 vampire template as the base. Keep its size, base attack, saves, skill points, d12 HD and applicable original powers. Constitution is absent. These age entries give the changes to Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha, speed and natural AC. Speed also specifies maximum horizontal movement while levitating. Damage reduction in every tier requires bamboo and magic to bypass. Apply one age row only. The sample above already incorporates its age. For unlisted save DCs use 10 + half HD, rounded down, + Cha modifier. The two spell-like abilities use 15 + Cha modifier instead. Claw damage follows the size table if the base creature has no claw attack. Where the printed example differs, use its own attack line.

Mature. Abilities +8/+4/+2/+4/+4. Speed +10 ft., DR 15, fast healing 5, turn resistance +4, natural AC +6, CR +2.
Old. Abilities +8/+6/+4/+4/+6. Speed +10 ft., DR 15, fast healing 6, turn resistance +5, natural AC +7, CR +3.
Ancient. Abilities +10/+6/+4/+6/+6. Speed +20 ft., DR 20, fast healing 6, turn resistance +6, natural AC +7, CR +3.
Eminent. Abilities +10/+8/+6/+6/+8. Speed +20 ft., DR 20, fast healing 8, turn resistance +7, natural AC +8, CR +4.
Patriarch. Abilities +12/+10/+8/+8/+10. Speed +30 ft., DR 25, fast healing 10, turn resistance +8, natural AC +8, CR +5.

lines: 7 + 7 × the caregiver’s level in hit points, with one d8 Hit Die per caregiver level.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A winged guardian with three heads, a lion, a ram and a dragon, and a scaled tail.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor 13 + PB. Constitution save +2 + PB. Athletics +3 + PB. Immune to Frightened. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11.

gm.title: Caregiver scaling
lines: PB is the caregiver’s proficiency bonus.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Signature Attack (Bite). Melee weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1d6 + PB piercing damage.

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Ram’s Defense (2 Ferocity). Make a signature attack. A hit gives the target disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of the chimera’s next turn.
Level 3, Lion’s Leap (5 Ferocity). The chimera moves up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. If it ends on the ground, each creature within 5 ft. makes a Strength save against DC 10 + PB or falls Prone.
Level 5, Volcanic Blow (8 Ferocity). Choose a visible point within 60 ft. Each creature in a 10-ft.-radius sphere around the point makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB. It takes PBd6 fire damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Protective Absorption (short or long rest). When the caregiver takes damage within 60 ft. of the chimera, the chimera can use its reaction to take half that damage in the caregiver’s place, rounded up.

gm.title: Mystic connection
lines: Defensive Eruption. At 9th level, a Beastheart with this companion and Mystic Connection can spend a bonus action once per long rest to unleash a burst of energy. Each enemy within 30 ft. makes a Dexterity save against the Beastheart’s exploit save DC. On a failure it takes 4d6 fire damage and falls Prone. On a success it takes half damage. The Beastheart and allies within 30 ft. have advantage on their next attack roll before the start of the Beastheart’s next turn.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Description
lines: A clockwork bodyguard that wants to be human. Its flourishes keep opponents off balance, but each damaging strike spends some of the time left in its springs.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Very rare. Solitary. Active any time. No food. Very to exceptional intelligence (11–16). Fearless morale (19–20). Height 6 feet. No magic resistance. A destroyed automaton yields Q × 2 in gems and 1d4 × 1,000 gp in precious metal.

gm.title: Hit Dice, THAC0 and XP
lines:
5 HD: THAC0 15, 650 XP.
6 HD: THAC0 15, 975 XP.
7 HD: THAC0 13, 1,400 XP.
8 HD: THAC0 13, 2,000 XP.
9–10 HD: THAC0 11, adding 1,000 XP per HD above 8.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Weapons. Two attacks by weapon with +1 to hit and +3 damage for effective Strength 18. It usually carries a rapier and main-gauche or a saber and stiletto. There is a 20% chance it also has a wheellock pistol. Each point of damage it deals costs one hour of activity.
Additional action. Roll d100 each round. 01–25 fancy move, parry as a 10th-level fighter and improve AC by 6. 26–45 amusing quip, same parry and a taunt against one target. 46–60 salute or disarm. The salute gives allies +1 to attack for one round per Hit Die. 61–75 compliment, an opposite-sex target saves vs. spell or comes under charm person. 76–90 embarrassing maneuver, make a called shot at no penalty and follow a success with an amusing quip. 91–100 bold fencing attack, gain +2 to attack this round and force the foe back 1d10 steps. Ignore that last result when fewer than 50 hours remain.

gm.title: Skills and defenses
lines: Use the abilities and nonweapon proficiencies of a swashbuckler of level equal to HD, with no fighting school. Proficiency checks succeed on 18 or less. Immune to mind-influencing magic such as charm person and suggestion. ESP and telepathy can still affect it. If exposed to moisture, save vs. poison or take 6d6 damage 1d4 days later. It fears rust monsters.

gm.title: Winding
lines: Maximum runtime is 10 hours per HP, then it goes dormant. Roll d100 for the percentage remaining when encountered, with a 10% minimum. Below 50%, it heads back to its creator. Rewinding restores one hour per round. Attempting to wind it fully has a 10% chance of destroying it. Only its creator can repair it, and it cannot be raised. It cannot rewind itself. Models of at least 9 HD often need a magical key kept by their maker.

gm.title: Variants
lines: A host to a heroic spirit can rewind itself upon obtaining its key. The spirit can stay until the mechanism rusts. A rogue automaton hosts a legacy leech, can rewind without a key, and uses effective Strength 19. It keeps its swashbuckler abilities and can use Legacies its symbiont shares. Ordinary swordsmen neither gain Legacies nor require cinnabryl.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The 46–60 result lists disarm as an option without adding a special disarm procedure.

gm.title: Description
lines: A murder victim’s spirit waits over its body until someone sees the glow in its dead eyes and becomes a witness to the killing.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +3. AC components +3 Dex, +2 deflection. Touch AC 15, flat-footed AC 12. Base attack +3, grapple +3 as listed. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +2, Ref +4, Will +8.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Incorporeal touch +5 (1d6 spiritual flame damage).
Control Flame (Su). Take hold of a nearby flame and make someone see the killer’s face in fire. A tendril from the fire can reach up to 10 ft., deal 1d6 damage, or ignite flammable material.
Death Vision (Su). The first person to look into the corpse’s eyes makes a DC 16 Will save. Success gives immunity to this power for one day. On failure, the person relives the victim’s last moments in a trance, which often calls for a Ravenloft Horror save. They see who killed the victim and feel driven to bring the killer to justice.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Incorporeal subtype, undead traits, +2 turn resistance. The spirit is naturally invisible. Magic that reveals invisible or ethereal creatures can show it as mist over its body or as an image of the dead person riding its chosen agent’s shoulders. The agent’s eyes glow slightly in the dark.

gm.title: Skills and feats

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land and underground. Solitary. Usually chaotic neutral. No treasure. Advancement 8–12 HD (Medium).

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Stealth +3. Immune to poison damage, Exhaustion, and Poisoned. Blindsight 30 ft. and blind beyond that radius. Passive Perception 9. Understands the languages it knew in life and cannot speak.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claw (group attack). Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. Hit 1 piercing damage. If at least three claws took part, the target must pass a DC 10 Constitution save or contract gravefilth.
Gravefilth halves healing granted by spells, powers, and comparable supernatural effects. The infected creature can repeat the DC 10 Constitution save after each long rest and recovers on a success.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: Magenta veins give away this crawling ivy. It clings to walls and waits until prey is close enough to wrap in its vines.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any temperate or warm land. Solitary. Always neutral. No treasure. Advancement 9–31 HD (Huge), 32+ HD (Gargantuan).

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +0. AC −2 size, −2 Dex, +1 natural, touch 6, flat-footed 9. Base attack and grapple +6. Space 10 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +6, Ref +2, Will +4.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Plant traits and DR 5/bludgeoning or slashing.
Camouflage (Ex). Notice it before it attacks with DC 16 Spot, Survival, or Knowledge (plants or herbs).
Tremorsense (Ex). Locate anything touching the ground within 60 ft. and distinguish the vibrations of individual creatures.
Dispersed Vines (Ex). Cover one 5-by-5-ft. square per HD, on the ground or on a wall. Track each die’s HP separately. A section at 0 HP or with a comparable loss such as a negative level cannot act. At −10 HP it is destroyed. An area attack deals full damage to every section it reaches.
Berries (Ex). Autumn berries can establish new colonies. They produce 2d8 flowers per HD. Press one flower to a wound to stabilize a dying creature or stop bleeding. Each flower works once and can also be used to make a curing potion.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Entangle (Ex). As a standard action, entangle all foes within reach as a 5th-level casting of entangle, Reflex DC 16. Creatures climbing the ivy lose their Dex bonus on this save.
Blood Drain (Ex). Deal 1d3 Con damage each round a victim remains entangled. A victim at Con 0 dies. The ivy loses 1 HD each week it drains less than 1 point of Con per HD.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: To distribute the printed 36 HP across eight sections without rolling, use four sections at 4 HP and four at 5 HP. The printed +0 initiative and flat-footed AC 9 are retained.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +7. AC components +3 Dex, +2 natural. Touch AC 13, flat-footed AC 12. Base attack +1, grapple +3. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +3, Will +4.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +2 melee (1d4 + 3).
Full attack. Two claws +2 melee (1d4 + 3 each) and bite −3 melee (1d8 + 2).
Blood Poisoning (Ex). An adjacent attacker who hits makes a DC 14 Reflex save to avoid a splash. A living attacker splashed then makes a DC 13 Fortitude save or takes 1 damage each round until death or treatment with neutralize poison or an equivalent effect.
Burning Blood (Su). The bite transmits a supernatural disease on a failed DC 13 Fortitude save. After a 1-day incubation, it deals 1 Constitution drain. Standard recovery saves do not end it. It continues until the victim dies at Constitution 0 or receives remove disease or similar magic.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Undead traits, DR 5/bludgeoning, cold immunity. It can be turned but cannot be rebuked or commanded by evil clerics. Sithkin changelings or arcane casters using control undead can control it. It does not understand or speak languages.

gm.title: Description
lines: A harpy matriarch who fights in flight with an electrified javelin.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Con +5, Wis +5. Acrobatics +11, Deception +7, Perception +8. Immune to lightning and thunder. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 16. Abyssal.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Keen Sight. Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. She can use Frightful Screech, then make two Talons attacks or one Javelin attack.
Talons. Melee weapon attack +8, reach 5 ft., one target, 11 (1d10 + 5) slashing.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack +8, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target, 9 (1d6 + 5) piercing plus 14 (4d6) lightning.
Frightful Screech. Chosen creatures within 120 ft. that are not Deafened must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or become Frightened for 1 minute. While affected, a creature must Dash and flee by the safest route on each turn if possible. It repeats the save whenever it ends a turn out of her line of sight. A successful save or the end of the effect grants immunity to her screech for 24 hours.
Thunder Blast (recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 15-ft. cube make a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 14 (4d6) thunder damage, getting pushed 10 ft., and falling Prone on failure. On success they only take half damage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Aerial Acrobat. Dash, Disengage, or Dodge.

gm.title: Description
lines: A crimson dragon stalks the cursed lands for cinnabryl. It often feints or puts on a display of Legacies before committing to a fight.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Solitary. Very rare in cursed lands. Active by day. Carnivore. Genius intelligence (17–18). Fanatic morale (17–18). All speak a dragon dialect other crimson and evil dragons understand. The chance of communicating with any intelligent creature starts at 15% for a hatchling and rises 5 percentage points per later age category.

gm.title: Age tiers
lines:
1. Hatchling, 0–5 years. 7 HD, AC 0, THAC0 13, combat modifier +1. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure none, 2,000 XP. Body 2–16 ft., tail 4–16 ft.
2. Very Young, 6–15 years. 9 HD, AC -1, THAC0 11, combat modifier +2. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure none, 3,000 XP. Body 16–27 ft., tail 16–25 ft.
3. Young, 16–25 years. 11 HD, AC -2, THAC0 9, combat modifier +3. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure B, 5,000 XP. Body 27–42 ft., tail 25–34 ft.
4. Juvenile, 26–50 years. 13 HD, AC -3, THAC0 7, combat modifier +4. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure BI, 8,000 XP. Body 42–61 ft., tail 34–53 ft.
5. Young Adult, 51–100 years. 14 HD, AC -4, THAC0 7, combat modifier +5. Fear 15 yd., save +3. Magic resistance 20%. Spells none. Treasure BI, 10,000 XP. Body 61–80 ft., tail 53–72 ft.
6. Adult, 101–200 years. 15 HD, AC -5, THAC0 5, combat modifier +6. Fear 20 yd., save +2. Magic resistance 25%. Spells 1 wizard. Treasure BH, 12,000 XP. Body 80–99 ft., tail 72–91 ft.
7. Mature Adult, 201–400 years. 16 HD, AC -6, THAC0 5, combat modifier +7. Fear 25 yd., save +1. Magic resistance 30%. Spells 2 wizard. Treasure BH, 13,000 XP. Body 99–118 ft., tail 91–110 ft.
8. Old, 401–600 years. 17 HD, AC -7, THAC0 5, combat modifier +8. Fear 30 yd., save +0. Magic resistance 35%. Spells 2/1 wizard. Treasure BHU, 14,000 XP. Body 118–137 ft., tail 110–129 ft.
9. Very Old, 601–800 years. 18 HD, AC -8, THAC0 5, combat modifier +9. Fear 35 yd., save −1. Magic resistance 40%. Spells 2/2 wizard. Treasure BHU, 15,000 XP. Body 137–157 ft., tail 129–148 ft.
10. Venerable, 801–1,000 years. 19 HD, AC -9, THAC0 5, combat modifier +10. Fear 40 yd., save −2. Magic resistance 45%. Spells 2/2/1 wizard, 1 priest. Treasure BH + U × 2, 16,000 XP. Body 157–177 ft., tail 148–168 ft.
11. Wyrm, 1,001–2,000 years. 20 HD, AC -10, THAC0 5, combat modifier +11. Fear 45 yd., save −3. Magic resistance 50%. Spells 2/2/2 wizard, 2 priest. Treasure BH + U × 2, 18,000 XP. Body 177–197 ft., tail 168–188 ft.
12. Great Wyrm, 1,200+ years. 21 HD, AC -11, THAC0 5, combat modifier +12. Fear 50 yd., save −4. Magic resistance 55%. Spells 3/2/2/1 wizard, 2/1 priest. Treasure BH + U × 3, 20,000 XP. Body 197–217 ft., tail 188–208 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws and bite. Two claws at 1d8 each and a bite at 4d6. Add the age tier’s combat modifier to each physical damage roll. Claws can strike the front and sides, and the bite also reaches behind. The dragon saves as a fighter of level equal to HD.
Cinnabryl breath. From Juvenile onward, the dragon can breathe once every three rounds, giving up its other attacks that round. It produces a 100-foot cone measuring 5 feet wide at its mouth and 50 feet across at the far end. It depletes all cinnabryl and ruins crimson essence in the cone. The dragon has a cumulative 3% chance per ounce depleted to gain one new Legacy. The cone does not increase with age.

gm.title: Other dragon attacks
lines:
Kick. Against a target behind it, deal claw damage. The target rolls Dexterity or lower on 1d20 or is pushed 1d6 feet plus 1 foot per age tier. A pushed target saves vs. petrification with the combat modifier as a penalty or falls. Use one hind leg if also attacking with a claw. No tail slap in the same round.
Snatch. From Young Adult, dive to grab a target at least two sizes smaller. On a hit there is a 50% chance of pinning its arms. The dragon can drop it, deal automatic claw damage each round, or transfer it to its jaws with another successful attack roll for automatic bite damage each round. Old dragons can snatch two targets. Wyrms and Great Wyrms can carry three by transferring one to the mouth.
Wing buffet. From Young Adult, deal claw damage against a target at either side. It falls unless it rolls at or below Dexterity on 1d20.
Tail slap. From Adult, attack up to the age-tier number of targets at the rear and sides, rolling separately. Each hit deals twice claw damage, and the target saves vs. petrification at a penalty equal to the combat modifier or is stunned for 1d4 + 1 minutes. It can smash light wood or drain a cube of force by one charge per two points of combat modifier, rounded down.
Stall. Hover one round near the ground, then land. During the stall, the dragon can attack with all four legs and its bite, or breathe instead. Debris creates a dust cloud out to the fear radius for one round in suitable terrain. Anyone in it is blinded and cannot cast.
Optional plummet. From at least 30 feet above the target, land on up to the combat-modifier number of targets, rolling separately for bite damage. Each hit target saves vs. petrification at a penalty equal to the modifier or is pinned and takes the damage again on the next round if the dragon holds it down. It must save again to escape an ongoing pin. The dragon cannot do anything else while plummeting or holding the pin.

gm.title: Fear and spellcasting
lines:
From Young Adult, seeing it causes targets under 1 HD and nonaggressive noncarnivores below the dragon’s HD to panic for 4d6 rounds. Other creatures below its HD in a charging dragon’s fear radius or under its flight path at up to 250 feet altitude save vs. petrification with the listed modifier. Failure gives −2 to attack and damage. Creatures at least equal to its HD are immune.
Determine its spells from the age tier. A dragon generally casts each spell once per day or more if rolled more than once. Casting is verbal only with casting time 1. It cannot attack, breathe, use innate magic, or do more than glide while casting.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: The first Legacy requires the dragon to drain at least 1 ounce of cinnabryl with its breath. Juvenile and older dragons are assumed to have 1d4 − 1 random Legacies for each age category from Juvenile onward. Duplicate Legacies stack if possible. Otherwise roll again. Add 1,000 XP per Legacy. A new Legacy costs no ability points. Physical changes appear over a few days, and the dragon can reverse them over the following week.

gm.title: Harvested scales
lines: One hide yields enough cinnabryl-bearing scales for at most one set of armor. A crimson essence alchemist must treat the scales into scale mail using at least one potion of crimson essence. It protects only the wearer. A slashing, piercing, or magical hit dealing more than 15 damage calls for an appropriate item saving throw. On failure the scales lose their protection in a smokepowder-like detonation.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Choose an age tier before play. The printed Wyrm and Great Wyrm age ranges overlap.

The spell totals list slots by spell level. The appendix gives no direct HP damage for the cinnabryl breath. General dragon attacks, fear, and casting follow the Monstrous Manual, Dragons, General. THAC0 uses Dungeon Master Guide Table 39.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Bite +13 melee (1d2 plus implant) or spit seed +4 ranged (1 damage plus implant).
Full attack. 4d4 bites at +16 melee, or 4d4 spit seeds at +4 ranged. Use the actual head count once established. Each head has 1d6 seeds. Spit seeds have a maximum range of 30 ft. and no range increment.
Implant Seeds (Ex). A bite or spit hit plants a seed. DC 15 Spot notices the numbed wound. DC 10 Heal removes the seed during the first 24 hours. After that it takes root in a humanoid and deals cumulative damage of 1d4 on day one, 2d4 on day two, and so on to 10d4 per day. A rooted seed requires DC 15 + days since rooting to remove with Heal. Every attempt deals half that day’s damage, even on a failure. If the victim dies with an implanted seed, a new tree grows from the body.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: Acererak and other demiliches of his tradition set soul gems into their skulls to feed their phylacteries.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Avoidance. If a saving throw would normally halve damage on a success, the demilich takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Turn Immunity. Immune to effects that turn Undead.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink or sleep. Use the printed 80 HP.
Enduring Existence. An intact phylactery restores the destroyed skull in 1d10 days. A demilich that still has the will to feed a soul to its phylactery can return to lich form by doing so.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Howl (Recharge 5–6). Every creature within 30 ft. that can hear the howl makes a DC 15 Constitution save. Failure drops it to 0 HP. Success leaves it Frightened until the end of its next turn.
Life Drain. Choose up to three visible creatures within 10 ft. Each makes a DC 19 Constitution save or takes 21 (6d6) necrotic damage. The demilich heals HP equal to the total damage dealt.
Trap Soul. Choose one visible creature within 30 ft. It makes a DC 19 Charisma save. On a failure, magic traps its soul in one of the demilich's gems and its body and carried equipment disappear. On a success, it takes 24 (7d6) necrotic damage, which still traps its soul if it brings the creature to 0 HP. The demilich devours an imprisoned soul after 24 hours. At 0 HP the demilich crumbles to powder and leaves its gems behind. Crushing a gem frees any soul still inside. Its body reforms in the nearest unoccupied space in the same state it was in when trapped.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Three legendary actions. Spend one option at the end of another creature’s turn. Regain spent actions at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Flight (1 action). Fly up to half its flying speed.
Cloud of Dust (1 action). Each creature within 10 ft., even around a corner, makes a DC 15 Constitution save or is Blinded until the end of the demilich’s next turn. On a success that creature is immune to this effect until the end of the demilich’s next turn.
Energy Drain (2 actions). Every creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, reduce maximum HP by 10 (3d6). A target dies if its maximum falls to 0. Greater Restoration or similar magic can restore the lost maximum.
Vile Curse (3 actions). One visible creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On failure it is magically cursed and has disadvantage on attack rolls and saves. It repeats the save at the end of each turn and ends the curse on success.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
In its lair, the demilich is CR 23 (50,000 XP). Act on initiative count 20, losing ties. No lair action while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before the first turn if surprised. Roll a d20. On 11 or higher, choose an effect. Never repeat the same effect on consecutive rounds.
Tremor. Each creature on the tomb floor makes a DC 19 Dexterity save or falls Prone.
Antimagic. Choose one visible creature within 60 ft. Antimagic Field fills its space and moves with it until initiative count 20 next round.
Seal Healing. Choose any number of visible creatures within 30 ft. They cannot regain HP until initiative count 20 next round.

gm.title: Lair traits
lines:
Use any of these optional tomb traits. A non-evil creature takes 16 (3d10) necrotic damage the first time it enters. Monsters in the tomb have advantage on saves against Charmed, Frightened and turning. A ward prevents unauthorized creatures from using teleportation or planar travel to enter or leave, but allows such movement entirely within the tomb.
After the demilich is destroyed, these effects fade over 10 days.

lines: A fiendish spider that can pull prey into its web and spray venom when badly wounded.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Dexterity saves +7. Perception +3, Stealth +7. Resists cold, fire and lightning. Immune to poison damage and the Poisoned condition. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 13. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Spider Climb. Move across difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
Web Walker. Webbing does not restrict its movement.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Stinger attack, or use Web Spinner and then make one melee attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +7 within 5 ft. Hit for 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing. The target then makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On failure it takes 27 (6d8) poison damage and is Poisoned for 1 minute. Success halves the poison damage and avoids the condition. If the poison damage drops it to 0 HP, it stabilizes and is Poisoned for 1 hour even if it regains HP. It is Paralyzed while that longer poison lasts.
Stinger. Melee weapon attack +7 within 5 ft. Hit for 9 (1d12 + 3) piercing. The target must pass a DC 14 Constitution save or be Paralyzed for 1 minute. Repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the condition on a success.
Web Spinner. Ranged weapon attack +7 with a 40-ft. range. On a hit, pull the target 40 ft. toward the spider and Grapple it (escape DC 14). Only one creature at a time can be held by Web Spinner. The spider can spend an action to cocoon that creature. The cocoon leaves it Restrained and ends the grapple.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Arterial Spray. When the spider takes damage while below half its maximum HP, it can spray venomous blood in a 15-ft. cone. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 14 Constitution save. Failure deals 13 (3d8) poison damage and leaves it Poisoned for 1 minute. Success halves the damage and avoids the poison condition. If the spray’s poison damage drops it to 0 HP, it stabilizes and is Poisoned for 1 hour even if it regains HP. It is Paralyzed while that longer poison lasts.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: Use the separate Demonfeed Spiderling block for the younger creatures in its nest.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed cocoon rule specifies no separate escape DC or duration.

lines: Senmet’s undead servants swim beneath the sands of Har’Akir, leaving shallow furrows when they travel near the surface.

lines: Initiative +2. AC 15, touch 10, flat-footed 15. The listed armor component is +3 natural. Base attack +1, grapple +2. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +0, Ref +1, Will +3. Swim (sand) +5. Improved Natural Armor.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Slam +2 melee for 1d8 + 1 damage. The prose gives the same damage for weapons or other attacks.
Grab from Beneath (Ex). From under the sand, make an attack against AC that includes the victim’s Dexterity bonus but excludes natural armor and worn armor. A hit grabs the victim. The victim can break free with an opposed Strength check. After 3 rounds of being pulled down, the victim is completely buried. They survive the first round underground and die at the end of the second unless freed.
Spell Use. A zombie that cast spells in life still casts them, using the sorcerer class regardless of its previous casting class.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Darkvision 60 ft., damage reduction 5/slashing, undead traits. Sandswim (Ex) lets it travel beneath the sand to set up a grab. The print supplies no separate sand movement speed. It understands simple commands and rarely speaks.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Deserts of Har’Akir, commonly in packs of 6–10. Usually neutral evil. No treasure. The prose says it retains its former skills and abilities. The printed stat block presents an ordinary specimen.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Preserve the listed AC and saves where the components and ability scores disagree. The grab gives a custom defense and escape check but prints no separate attack bonus. Use the printed slam bonus for the initial grab as a table default.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Saving Throws Wis +9, Cha +9 Skills Insight +9, Perception +9 Damage Resistances radiant; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks Condition Immunities charmed, exhaustion, frightened Senses darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 19 Languages all, telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Angelic Weapons. The deva’s weapon attacks are magical. When the deva hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4d8 radiant damage (included in the attack). Innate Spellcasting. The deva’s spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 17). The deva can innately cast the following spells, requiring only verbal components: At will: detect evil and good 1/day each: commune, raise dead Magic Resistance. The deva has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The deva makes two melee attacks. Mace. Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) radiant damage. Healing Touch (3/Day). The deva touches another creature. The target magically regains 20 (4d8 + 2) hit points and is freed from any curse, disease, poison, blindness, or deafness. Change Shape. The deva magically polymorphs into a humanoid or beast that has a challenge rating equal to or less than its own, or back into its true form. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the new form (the deva’s choice). In a new form, the deva retains its game statistics and ability to speak, but its AC, movement modes, Strength, Dexterity, and special senses are replaced by those of the new form, and it gains any statistics and capabilities (except class features, legendary actions, and lair actions) that the new form has but that it lacks.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A wiry horned devil clerk in a blue-gray coat carrying an open ledger and quill.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Chain shirt. Fire damage immunity. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 12. Common and Infernal.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Importunity. At the start of its turn, the notary can bless a visible non-minion ally within 60 ft. without spending an action. The ally can add +1 to its next attack roll or saving throw before the start of the notary’s next turn. Blessings from multiple notaries stack to a maximum bonus of +5.
Minion. Damage from an attack or failed save drops the notary to 0 HP. Other damage kills it if it deals at least 13 damage. It ignores smaller amounts from those other effects.
True Name. If the notary hears someone within 60 ft. speak its true name, it loses its damage immunity and Importunity for 24 hours.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Brimstone (Group Attack). Melee or ranged spell attack +6, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft., one target. Hit 4 fire damage.

gm.title: Minion rules
lines:
Group attack. Two to five notaries on the same turn can each spend an action to attack a target in reach or range of every participant. Make one roll at +6 plus the number joining. A hit deals 4 fire damage per participant. A solo notary attacks at +6. Advantage or disadvantage applies if all participants have it. When cover or concealment differs, roll separately for each group. The target chooses which participant is affected by a response that can affect only one attacker.
Group opportunity attack. If a target provokes from multiple notaries at once, each can spend its reaction to join the melee Brimstone attack. Notaries have no Hit Dice and cannot score critical hits.
Overkill. A weapon hit dealing more than 13 damage leaves surplus that can drop an eligible additional notary to 0 HP for each 13 points of surplus damage or part thereof. For melee, each must be within reach of the weapon. At range, each must lie on the line from attacker through the first target and within the weapon’s short range. This rule excludes opportunity attacks.

gm.title: Description
lines: A foot-tall toy stands still until its painted expression twists and it lunges.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +2. AC +2 size, +4 Dex, +2 natural. Touch AC 16, flat-footed AC 14. Base attack +5. Space 2½ ft., reach 0 ft. Fort +2, Ref +4, Will +2.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Bite +3 melee for 1d6 − 2 and Biting Laughter.
Biting Laughter (Su). A bite hit calls for a DC 13 Will save. On failure, the victim falls prone and cannot act as with Tasha's hideous laughter. The laughter lasts until dispelled at DC 17 or until the victim dies. It deals one negative level per round. After the effect is dispelled, remove one negative level per round.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Damage reduction 10/magic.
Magic Immunity (Ex). Immune to spells, spell-like abilities and supernatural effects, with named exceptions. Fire effects deal half damage on a failed save and none on a successful save. Warp wood slows it as the slow spell. Mending restores full HP. A targeted dispel magic at DC 15 disables it for a number of rounds equal to the caster's dispel check result minus 10. A result at least 10 above the DC destroys it. Detect magic reveals its aura returning while it is disabled.
Construct traits. Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, disease and similar effects. Critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability damage, energy drain and death from massive damage do not affect it, subject to the exceptions below.

gm.title: Dread golem commands
lines: The creator can give commands from within 60 ft. if the golem can see and hear them. It follows the last command and responds to attacks against it. Some dread golems act independently.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land or underground. Solitary, always neutral, no treasure. Advances to 8–10 HD (Small) or 11–14 HD (Medium).

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The source gives only +5 on the base attack/grapple line. A standard 3.5 grapple calculation yields −5 from base attack +5, Strength −2 and Tiny size −8. Initiative is printed as +2 despite Dexterity 19.

gm.title: Description
lines: A dolphin servant that swims through air just above the ground. Its humanoid form keeps its gills and webbed hands and feet.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any terrain and activity cycle. Very rare. Solitary, appearing alone. No diet or treasure. Neutral, or matches the bearer. Intelligence Genius (17–18). Size Medium, 5 ft. long. Morale Fearless (19–20). Magic resistance 15%.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Ram. In natural form, make one attack for 2d4 damage.
Humanoid weapons. Use any weapon available to a wizard at the listed THAC0.
Spellcasting. Cast as an 8th-level wizard in either active form. In natural form, dolphin speech and flipper gestures supply verbal and somatic components, but spells with material components are unavailable. The humanoid form can carry materials and often has two minor magic items. The bearer can supply a spellbook, which the servant absorbs on returning to natural form.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Saving throws. Use the saves of an 8th-level wizard.
Air movement. A magical field supports the natural form a few feet above the ground, where it moves as if swimming.
Speech. The humanoid form can still communicate with dolphins.

gm.title: Bearer benefits
lines: While in contact or personally carrying its arms, use the servant’s saving throws whenever they are better. While telepathically linked, the bearer can breathe water and cast any 1st-level spell known to the servant. The Baroness of Savaria is the known bearer.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printing leaves the spell selection to the referee. Prepare the available spells as for an 8th-level wizard.

gm.title: Description
lines: A tangle of vines grows pods large enough to hold a person. Victims can return to their companions with familiar memories and an allegiance to the plant.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Warm or temperate land. Solitary. Always chaotic evil. No treasure of its own. Podlings have standard treasure. Advancement 11–14 HD (Gargantuan), 15–20 HD (Colossal).

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +0. Vines AC 8 (−2 size), touch 10, flat-footed 8. Pods AC 16 (+6 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 16. Base attack and grapple are both +7. Space one 10-ft. square per HD, reach 0 ft. Fort +4, Will +4. Reflex is unlisted. Bluff +20, Diplomacy +18, Gather Information +18, Sense Motive +18. No feats.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Plant traits, DR 10/bludgeoning or slashing, electricity resistance 20 and fire resistance 20. Has no physical attacks. Each HD supplies one pod. The plant perceives and communicates through its continuous telepathic link to its podlings. The plant and all podlings share their languages and can use the highest available Int-, Wis-, and Cha-based skill bonus among them.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Mind Bondage (Su). Once per round, as a standard action, randomly select a sleeping or unconscious humanoid within 1 mile per plant HD. Will DC 14 + half the plant’s HD (DC 19 for the sample). Failure traps the soul in a vacant pod and gives the victim the podling quality. The attack is mind-affecting. Stop attempts for one day after a success. Each pod holds one soul, and no attempt is possible if all pods are occupied.
Dominate and duplicate. The combat text gives a separate on-site procedure. A humanoid entering the plant’s area must make a DC 25 Will save against its domination. On a failure the plant lures the victim into a pod that traps the soul, consumes the body at 1 HP per round, then releases a duplicate with the victim’s memories. The plant can use this domination through its clones to lure more victims.

gm.title: Podlings
lines: The plant controls a podling completely. The podling is otherwise immune to mind-affecting effects, retains its statistics and abilities except divinely granted powers, and acts as chaotic evil. Animal companions and similar bonds may detect the change. Starting 24 hours after capture, the podling loses 1d4 HP daily and cannot heal naturally. After piercing or slashing damage, it must make a Reflex save at DC 10 + damage or reveal its hollow interior. Witnesses may make a DC 15 Horror save. A podling that dies while enslaved has its life energy consumed, and only true resurrection can restore it.

gm.title: Dispersed Vines (Ex)
lines: Track HP per Hit Die. Put two HP from each HD into a shared vine and root pool and assign the rest of each die to its own pod. Area attacks deal full damage to each section in range. At 0 HP a pod deals nonlethal damage equal to its podling’s total HP + 10. At −10 HP the pod breaks, frees the soul, removes podling status, and costs the plant one HD. At 0 HP the vine pool stops pod communication and knocks out all podlings in the same way. At −10 HP the vines free every soul. The plant can also free all souls to feign destruction. Kill it by destroying the vine pool and every pod.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The combat paragraph gives DC 25 for dominating people in the patch. Mind Bondage has a separate range, target requirement, and DC formula. Both procedures are retained as printed.
For the listed 50 HP, use a 20-HP vine pool and ten 3-HP pods as a quick distribution. Per-HD rolls can vary individual pod HP.

gm.title: Description
lines: Taryon Darrington’s mechanical scribe and protector.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Dexterity saves +4, Constitution +5. Athletics +7, Perception +8. Immune to poison damage and Charmed, Exhaustion and Poisoned. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 18. Understands Taryon Darrington’s languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Arcane Surge (4/day). When Doty hits, Taryon Darrington can add 14 (4d6) force damage to the hit if Taryon is not Incapacitated.
Dedicated Servant. Includes 20 extra HP and grants +2 to saves, proficient ability checks and attack rolls.
Limited Vocabulary. The six Common words Doty can say are Tary, Yes, Correct, Absolutely, Soon and Handsome.
Vigilant. Doty cannot be Surprised.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Empowered Fist. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 5 ft. Hit for 8 (1d8 + 4) force.
Repair (3/day). Doty restores 15 (2d8 + 6) of its own HP.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Deflect. When an attacker Doty can see within 5 ft. attacks someone else, Doty can impose Disadvantage on the attack roll. The attacker also takes 6 (1d4 + 4) force damage.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: For commands, use the Doty trait and Multitask action in the Taryon Darrington stat block.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed Dexterity and Constitution saves are +4 and +5. Dedicated Servant separately grants a +2 bonus on saves without saying whether the listed saves already include it.

gm.title: Description
lines: A winged, many-tailed hydra made in an attempt to reproduce Tiamat’s power. Its five heads feed constantly and can pour their breath into a single cone.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Multiple Heads. The dracohydra starts with five heads. While it has more than one, it has advantage on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned or knocked unconscious. Whenever it takes 30 or more damage in one turn, one head dies. It dies if it loses all its heads. At the end of its turn, it grows two heads for each one that died since its last turn and regains 10 hit points per head grown. Radiant damage taken since its last turn prevents this regrowth.
Reactive Heads. For each head beyond the first, it has an extra reaction usable only for opportunity attacks.
Wakeful. At least one head stays awake while the dracohydra sleeps.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack per living head.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d10 + 5) damage. Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning or poison.
Prismatic Breath (Recharge 4–6). All heads exhale together in a 60-ft. cone. Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning or poison. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 17 Dexterity save, taking 33 (6d10) damage of that type on a failure or half as much on a success.

While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.
